column1: These are the names of the ancestors of Jesus Christ.
He was a descendant of King David, and King David was a descendant of Abraham.
Abraham's son was Isaac, and Isaac's son was Jacob, and then Judah and his brothers were born from Jacob.
Judah's sons were Perez and Zerah.
(The name of the mother of Perez and Zerah was Tamar.
) Perez's son was Hezron.
Hezron's son was Ram, 4 Ram's son was Amminadab.
Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon was the father of Salmon, 5 Salmon's son was Boaz.
(The name of Boaz's mother was Rahab.
) Boaz and Ruth were the parents of Obed, and Obed's son was Jesse.
And Jesse's son was King David.
(King Solomon was David's son.
) He was born from the woman who had previously been Uriah's wife, 7 Solomon's son was Rehoboam.
And Rehoboam's son was Abijah.
And Abijah was the father of Asa.
Asa's son was Jehoshaphat.
Then Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram, and Joram was the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah's son was Jotham, and Jotham was the son of Ahaz.
Then Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh.
Manasseh's son was Amon, and Amon was the father of Josiah.
Then, at the time when the Israelites were taken captive and carried away to the land of Babylon, Josiah was the father of Jeconiah and his brothers.
After they had been taken to the land of Babylon, Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel, and then Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud, Abiud was the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim was the father of Azor.
Azor's son was Zadok.
Zadok was the father of Achim, and Achim was the father of Eliud.
Eliud's son was Eleazar.
And Eleazar was the son of Matthan.
Matthan's son was Jacob.
And Jacob was the father of Joseph, who was Mary's husband.
And Mary gave birth to Jesus, who is called Christ.

Thus, there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen generations from David until the Israelites were taken captive and sent to Babylon, and fourteen more generations from the time the Israelites were taken captive and sent to Babylon until Christ.

The Birth of Christ 18 The birth of Jesus Christ happened in this way: when his mother Mary was engaged to Joseph, before they were married, it was discovered that she was pregnant through the power of the Holy Spirit.
But her husband Joseph was a righteous man and did not want to disgrace her, so he decided to leave her secretly.

While he was thinking about these things, an angel of God came to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, descendant of David! Do not be afraid to take your wife Mary into your home, because the child she carries in her womb is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son, and you shall name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”

” 22 All this happened so that the word that the Lord had spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: 23 “Look, a virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and his name will be called Immanuel,” which means, “God is with us.”
” 24 Then Joseph woke up from sleep and, according to the command of the angel of God, took Mary as his wife and brought her into his home.
And he did not have relations with her until she gave birth to a son, and Joseph named the child Jesus.
When King Herod was ruling over the region of Judea, Jesus was born in the town of Bethlehem in that region.
Some time later, several wise men who had knowledge of the stars came from the east to the city of Jerusalem.
They came asking, “Where is the king of the Jews who has been born? We saw his star in the eastern direction, which tells about his birth, and therefore we have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard this, he and all the people of Jerusalem with him became worried.

Then he gathered all the chief priests and teachers of the Scriptures and asked them, “What does the Holy Scripture say? Where should Christ be born?” 5 They told him, “In the town of Bethlehem in the region of Judea,” because this was written in the Holy Scripture through the prophets: 6 “O town of Bethlehem, you who are in the land of Judah, you are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah.
Because from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.”
” 7 Herod wanted to know how old the child was, so he secretly called the men who had knowledge of the stars and asked them exactly when the star had appeared.
And the king sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and find out exactly about the child, and when you find him, let me know, so that I too may come and worship him.”
” 9 After hearing the king's words, they left, and the star that they had seen in the east went ahead of them.
And when it reached the place where the child was, it stopped above the house.
He saw the star and was very happy that it had stopped above the house.
They went into the house and saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshipped the child. Then they opened their bags and offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Then God warned them in a dream not to go back to King Herod, so they returned to their country by another road without telling the king.
Going to Egypt 13 After the wise men had left, an angel of God appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up! Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt.
Stay there until I tell you to leave.
Because King Herod wants to search for this child and kill him.
” 14 So Joseph got up that very night and took the child and his mother and left for Egypt.
And he stayed there until the death of King Herod.
This happened so that the word spoken by the Lord through the prophet Hosea might be fulfilled: “I called my son out of Egypt.”
” Herod kills the young children 16 When King Herod saw that the wise men had deceived him, he became very angry.
He sent soldiers and, according to the time he had learned exactly from the wise men, had all the boys in the town of Bethlehem and the surrounding areas who were two years old or younger killed.
Then the word spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled, 18 “A voice was heard in the town of Ramah, crying and great mourning.
Rachel was crying for her children and did not want to be comforted, because they were dead.

” Coming from Egypt 19 After King Herod died, an angel of God spoke to Joseph in a dream while he was in Egypt, 20 “Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, because King Herod and the people who wanted to kill the child are dead.”
” 21 Joseph woke up and took the child and his mother with him and returned to the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was ruling over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there.
Then, after receiving a warning from God in a dream, he went to the region of Galilee.
And he went and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that the word spoken by the prophets about Jesus might be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
” In those days John the Baptist came and began preaching in the wilderness of Judea: 2 “Stop committing sins, because the kingdom of heaven has come near.
” 3 This is the one who was spoken about through the prophet Isaiah: “A voice of one calling out in the wilderness: Prepare the way for the Lord and make his paths straight.
” 4 John wore clothes made of camel's hair and wore a leather belt around his waist.
His food was locusts and honey.
Then people from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and all the areas around the Jordan River came to him.
They confessed their sins and were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

When he saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to him to be baptized, he said, “You brood of snakes! How will you escape the punishment of hell? 8 Therefore, if you have truly stopped committing sins, then do good works to show it.
And do not think in your hearts that our father is Abraham.
Because I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
The axe has already been placed at the root of the trees, so every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
This means that God will punish all those who do not stop committing sins.
“I baptize you with water so that you may turn away from your sins, but the one who comes after me is more powerful than I am.
I am not even worthy to carry his sandals.
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly clean his threshing floor and gather his grain into his storehouse, but he will burn the chaff with a fire that can never be put out.”

But John tried to stop him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and yet you have come to me?” 15 Jesus answered him, “Let it be so for now, because it is right for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.
” Then he agreed to what Jesus said.
And when Jesus was baptized and came up out of the water, heaven opened, and he saw the Holy Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
And behold, a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am very pleased.

He remained there for forty days and forty nights without eating or drinking, and afterward he became hungry.
Then Satan came to him and said, “If you are the Son of God, prove it by commanding these stones to become bread so that you can eat them.

’” 5 Then Satan took him to the holy city of Jerusalem and made him stand on the highest point of the temple.
And he said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down and prove it.
Because it is written in the Holy Scriptures: He will command his angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands so that your feet will never strike against a stone.”
” 7 Jesus said to him, “It is also written in the Holy Scriptures: ‘You must not test the Lord your God.’
’” 8 Then Satan took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, 9 and said to him, “If you bow down and worship me, I will give you everything.”
” 10 Then Jesus said to him, “Go away, Satan! It is written in the Holy Scriptures: Worship the Lord your God and serve only him.”
” 11 Then Satan left him, and behold, angels came and began serving him.

Light shone upon those who were living in a place where there was always the danger of death.”

” The Calling of the First Disciples

While Jesus was walking along the shore of the Sea of Galilee in the region of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who was called Peter, and his brother Andrew, casting a net into the sea, because they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you people who gather other people so that they may become my disciples.”
” 20 They immediately left their nets and followed him to become his disciples.
Going farther from there, Jesus saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and his brother John.
They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, repairing their nets.
Jesus called them too.
They immediately left the boat and their father and followed him to become his disciples.
Healing the Sick in the Region of Galilee
Jesus traveled throughout the region of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the good news of the kingdom, and healing every kind of disease and weakness among the people.

His fame spread throughout the whole region of Syria, and people brought to him all the sick who were suffering from various diseases and pains, those who had evil spirits, those with epilepsy, and those suffering from paralysis, and he healed them.
Large crowds from the region of Galilee, the towns of the Decapolis, the city of Jerusalem, the region of Judea, and from across the Jordan River followed him.
When Jesus saw the crowd, he went up onto the mountain, and when he sat down, his disciples came to him.

Blessed are those who mourn, because they will receive peace from God.
Blessed are those who are humble, because through God they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst to live a righteous life, because God will satisfy them.
Blessed are those who show mercy, because God will also show mercy to them.
Blessed are those whose hearts are pure, because they will see God.
Blessed are those who make peace, because they will be called God's sons and daughters.
Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, because the kingdom of heaven belongs to them.

Then be happy and rejoice, because you have a great reward in heaven.

I tell you the truth, you will not get out of prison until you have paid every last penny.

And whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

Do not swear by your head either, because you cannot make even one hair white or black.
But let your word be ‘Yes’ if you mean yes, and ‘No’ if you mean no, because anything more than this comes from the devil.

Give to anyone who asks you, and do not turn away from anyone who wants to borrow from you.

So that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: 18 “Look, this is my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my heart is pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles.
“He will not quarrel with people, nor shout, and no one will hear his voice in the marketplaces.
“He will not break a bruised reed, nor will he extinguish a smoldering lamp; he will continue until he brings justice to victory.
“And the Gentiles will put their hope in his name.
” 22 Then some people brought to him a blind and mute man who had an evil spirit that prevented him from seeing and speaking, and he healed him, so that the mute man began to speak and see.

All the people were amazed and began to say, “Could this be the Son of David?” 24 But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “He drives out evil spirits with the help of Satan, the ruler of evil spirits.
” 25 Knowing their thoughts, he said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be destroyed, and no city or household divided against itself will stand.

And if Satan drives out Satan, he has become his own enemy; then how will his kingdom stand? 27 If I drive out evil spirits with the help of Satan, then with whose help do your people drive them out? Therefore, they themselves will judge you.
But if I drive out evil spirits by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come near you.
” 29 “How can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can rob his house.
” 30 “Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I tell you that every kind of sin and evil against people will be forgiven, but evil spoken against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
Whoever says something against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever says something against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this world or in the world to come.
” 33 “A tree is known by its fruit. If you call the tree good, then call its fruit good too; or if you call the tree bad, then call its fruit bad too.
You brood of snakes, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For whatever fills the heart comes out of the mouth.
A good person brings good things out of the good treasure of the heart, and an evil person brings evil things out of the evil treasure of the heart.
And I tell you that people will give an account on the day of judgment for every useless word they speak.
For by your words you will be declared innocent, and by your words you will be declared guilty.
” 38 At this, some scribes and Pharisees said to him, “Teacher, we want to see a miraculous sign from you.
” 39 He answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation looks for a sign, but no sign will be given to them except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
Just as the prophet Jonah was in the belly of a great fish for three nights and three days, so the Son of Man will be inside the earth for three nights and three days.

The people of Nineveh will rise with the people of this generation on the day of judgment and condemn them, because they accepted the preaching of the prophet Jonah and repented of their sins, and look, someone greater than Jonah is here.

The Queen of the South will rise with the people of this generation on the day of judgment and condemn them, because she came from the other end of the earth to hear the wisdom of King Solomon, and look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
” 43 “When an evil spirit leaves a person, it wanders through dry places looking for rest, but does not find any.
Then it says, ‘I will return to the same person from whom I came out.’
” And when it comes, it finds the person’s house swept clean and put in order.
Then the evil spirit goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they enter that person and live there, and the person’s final condition becomes worse than the first.
That is how it will also be with the evil people of this generation.
” 46 While he was still speaking to the crowd, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, wanting to speak with him.
Someone said to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to speak with you.

” 48 Hearing this, Jesus replied to the one who told him, “Who is my mother? And who are my brothers?” 49 And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, “Look, these are my mother and my brothers.
Because whoever does the will of my heavenly Father is my brother, my sister, and my mother.
” On that same day Jesus left the house and sat beside the Sea of Galilee.
And such a large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat, while the whole crowd stood on the shore.
And he taught them many things in parables: “A farmer went out to sow seed.
While he was sowing, some seeds fell along the roadside, and birds came and ate them.
Some seeds fell on rocky ground, where they did not have much soil, and because they did not have deep soil, they sprang up quickly.
But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they dried up.
Some seeds fell among thorns, and the thorns grew and choked them.
But some seeds fell on good soil and produced a crop, some a hundred times, some sixty times, and some thirty times.
Whoever has ears, let him listen carefully.

” 10 The disciples came near him and asked, “Why do you speak to the people in parables?” 11 He answered, “The understanding of the secrets of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.
Because whoever has something will be given more, and he will have plenty, but whoever has nothing, even what he has will be taken away from him.
I speak to them in parables because although they see, they do not truly see, and although they hear, they do not hear or understand.
” 14 “The prophecy of the prophet Isaiah about them is being fulfilled: ‘You will hear, but you will not understand, and you will see, but you will not perceive.

’” 15 “For the hearts of these people have become dull, and they hear with their ears without understanding, and they have closed their eyes, so that they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back, and I would heal them.
” 16 But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
I tell you the truth, many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear what you hear, but did not hear it.

“Now listen to the meaning of the parable of the sower. 19 Whoever hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it is like the seed that was sown along the roadside; the evil one comes and takes away what was sown in his heart.
And the seed sown on rocky ground is like the person who hears the word and immediately accepts it with joy.
But because he has no root within himself, he lasts only for a short time, and when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he immediately stumbles.
The seed sown among thorns is like the person who hears the word, but the worries of this world and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it produces no fruit.
The seed sown on good soil is like the person who hears and understands the word and produces fruit, some a hundred times, some sixty times, and some thirty times.
” 24 Jesus gave them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a farmer who sowed good seed in his field.
But while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.
When the plants sprouted and produced heads of grain, the weeds also appeared.
” 27 “The household servants came and said to him, ‘Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? Then where did the weeds come from?’” 28 “He said to them, ‘This is the work of an enemy.
’ The servants said, ‘Do you want us to go and gather the weeds?’” 29 “He said, ‘No, because while gathering the weeds you might pull up the wheat along with them.
Let both grow together until the harvest, and at harvest time I will tell the harvesters: First gather the weeds and tie them in bundles to burn them, and gather the wheat into my barn.’
” 31 He gave them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field.
It is smaller than all the other seeds, but when it grows, it becomes larger than all the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and make nests in its branches.
” 33 He told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast, which a woman took and mixed into three measures (fifteen kilograms) of flour, and eventually all the flour became leavened.
” 34 Jesus taught all these things to the people in parables, and he used parables to give this kind of teaching.
So that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “I will open my mouth to speak in parables; I will reveal things that have been hidden since the beginning of the world.
” 36 Then he left the crowd and went into the house, and his disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.
” 37 Jesus answered them, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world, the good seed is the children of the kingdom, and the weeds are the children of the evil one.
The enemy who sowed them is the devil.
The harvest is the end of the world, and the harvesters are the angels.
” 40 “Just as the weeds are gathered and burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of the world.
I will send my angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom everything that causes people to sin and those who encourage others to sin, and those who do evil deeds.
And they will throw them into the furnace of fire, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
At that time the righteous people will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
Whoever has ears, let him listen carefully.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid again, and in his joy he sold everything he had and bought that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant searching for fine pearls.
When he found one very expensive pearl, he went and sold everything he had and bought it.
Again, he said, the kingdom of heaven is like a large fishing net that is thrown into the sea and gathers fish of every kind.
When the net was full, the fishermen pulled it to the shore, and sitting down, they gathered the good fish into baskets but threw the bad ones away.
This is how it will be at the end of the world.
The angels will come and separate the wicked people from the righteous, 50 and the angels will throw the wicked people into the furnace of fire.
Where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
“Have you understood all these things?” They said to him, “Yes.
Jesus said to them, ‘Therefore, every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like the master of a house who brings out new and old things from his treasure.
” 53 When Jesus had spoken all these parables, he departed from there.

And coming to his own town Nazareth, he began to give them such teaching in their synagogue that they were astonished and began to say, “Where did he get this wisdom and these works of power? 55 Is this not the carpenter's son? And is not his mother's name Mary and his brothers' names James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas? 56 And do not all his sisters live among us? Then where did he get all this?” 57 In this way they stumbled because of him, but Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not dishonored anywhere except in his own village and home.”
” 58 And he did not do many miraculous works there because of their unbelief.

At that time, Herod the king of the Galilee region of the country heard the mention of Jesus, 2 and he said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist! He has risen alive from among the dead, which is why these works of power are seen from him.”
” 3 John had been caught, bound, and thrown into prison.

Because Herod had kept his brother Philip's wife Herodias with himself while he was alive, 4 because John had told him that keeping her was not right for you according to Moses's rules and regulations.
Therefore he wanted to kill him, but he was afraid of the people because they considered John to be a prophet.
But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias pleased Herod by dancing at the festival.
At this he swore an oath and promised, “Whatever you ask, I will give you.”
” 8 Prompted by her mother she said, “Have the head of John the Baptist brought to me here on a platter.”
” 9 The king became very sad, but because of his oath and those sitting with him, he ordered that it be given.
And he sent soldiers into the prison and had John's head cut off.
And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, who took it to her mother.
Then John's disciples came and took his body away and buried it, and went and gave the news to Jesus.
When Jesus heard this, he got into a boat and went away from there to a desolate place, in solitude.
Hearing this, people followed behind him on foot from town after town.
When Jesus reached the shore, he saw a large crowd and felt pity for them, and healed their sick.
When evening came, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a desolate place, and it is getting late, so dismiss the people so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.”
” 16 But Jesus said to them, “Their going is not necessary! You give them something to eat.”
” 17 They said to Jesus, “Here with us, except for five loaves of bread and two fish, there is nothing else.”
” 18 Jesus said, “Bring them here to me.

” 19 Then Jesus told the people to sit on the grass, and took those five loaves of bread and two fish; looking up towards heaven, he gave thanks to God for the food and breaking the bread gave it to the disciples, and the disciples to the people.
When all had eaten and were satisfied, the disciples picked up twelve baskets full of leftover pieces.
And those who ate were about five thousand men, excluding women and children.
Then he immediately made his disciples get into the boat so that they would go to the other side ahead of him, while he dismissed his people.
Having dismissed the people, he went up on the mountain by himself to pray; and until evening he was there alone.
By then the boat had gone very far from the shore of the sea and was tossing around, buffeted by the waves, because the wind was against it.
Around three o'clock in the morning, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
Seeing him walking on the sea, the disciples were terrified.
And said, “It is a ghost!” and started screaming out of fear.
Then Jesus immediately talked to them and said, “Take courage! It is I, do not be afraid!” 28 Peter answered him, “O Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you walking on the water.
” 29 Jesus said, “Come!” Then Peter got down from the boat and started walking on the water to go to Jesus.

But seeing the wind he got scared, and when he began to sink he cried out, saying, “O Lord, save me!” 31 Jesus immediately stretched out his hand, caught him, and said to him, “O you of little faith, why did you doubt?” 32 When they got into the boat, the wind stopped.
Seeing this event, his disciples who were on the boat praised him and said, “Truly, you are the Son of God.
” 34 Crossing the Sea of Galilee, they arrived in the region of Gennesaret.
The people of that place recognized him and sent word into all the surrounding country, and brought all the sick to him.
And begged him to let them touch just the edge of his clothes, and as many as touched him were healed.

Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from the city of Jerusalem and said, 2 “Why do your disciples ignore the traditions of the elders, why do they eat bread without washing their hands?” 3 He answered them, “Why do you also set aside God's command because of your traditions? 4 Because God said, ‘Respect your parents, and whoever speaks evil of parents, let him be put to death.

’ 5 But you say that if anyone says to his parents, ‘Whatever I was supposed to give to you from my property, I have dedicated to God’, 6 then he does not honor his father; in this way you have set aside the word of God because of your traditions.
O hypocrites, the prophet Isaiah predicted this correctly about you” 8 These people honor me with their lips, but their heart stays far from me.
“And they worship me in vain, because they teach human ways as religious doctrines.

” 10 Then he called the people to himself and said to them, “Listen, and understand 11 what goes into the mouth does not make a person unclean, but what comes out of the mouth, that very thing makes a person unclean.
” 12 Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees stumbled upon hearing this word?” 13 He answered, “Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted.
Let them go; they are blind guides, and if a blind man shows the way to a blind man, then both will fall into a pit.
” 15 Hearing this, Peter said to him, “Explain this example to us.

” 16 Jesus said to them, “Are you also still without understanding? 17 Do you not know that whatever goes into the mouth falls into the stomach, and comes out through the latrine? 18 But whatever comes out from the mouth comes out from the heart, and that very thing makes a person unclean.
Because evil thoughts, murder, adultery, going to another's woman, theft, false testimony, and wickedness come out from the heart itself.
These are what make a person unclean, but eating bread without washing hands does not make a person unclean.
” Faith of a Canaanite Woman from the Syrophoenician Region (Mar 7:24-30) 21 Jesus, leaving from there, went towards the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
A Canaanite woman came out from that region, and shouting out, started saying, “O Lord! Offspring of David, have mercy on me! An evil spirit torments my daughter very much.
” 23 But Jesus gave her no answer.
Then his disciples came and requested him, “Send her away, because she keeps coming behind us shouting.
” 24 Jesus answered, “Except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, I was not sent to anyone.
” 25 But she came, and bowing to Jesus, started saying, “O Lord, help me.
” 26 Jesus answered, “Taking the children's bread and throwing it in front of dogs is not right.
” 27 She said, “It is true, Lord, but even dogs under the table eat the pieces of children's bread.
” 28 Upon this, Jesus answered her, “O woman, your faith is firm.
As you wish, let it be so for you.
” And her daughter became well from that very hour.
Jesus came from there near the Sea of Galilee, and climbing up the mountain, sat down.
Then crowd after crowd came to him.
They brought along with them the lame, the blind, the maimed, the mute, and many other people to him, and laid them at his feet, and he healed them.
When the people saw that the mute speak, and the maimed are healed, and the lame walk, and the blind see, they were amazed and praised the God of Israel.
Jesus called his disciples and said, “I feel pity for this crowd, because they have been with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
I do not want to send them away hungry, lest they become exhausted and faint on the way.

” 33 The disciples said to him, “Where in this wilderness will we get so much bread to feed such a large crowd?” 34 Jesus asked them, “How many loaves of bread do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.
” 35 Then he commanded the people to sit on the ground.
And taking those seven loaves and the fish, giving thanks to God he broke them, and kept giving them to his disciples, and the disciples to the people.
In this way everyone ate and was satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven baskets of leftover pieces.
Excluding women and children, there were four thousand men who ate.
When he sent the crowd away, he got into the boat and came to the border of Magadan country.
The Pharisees and Sadducees came near to test him and said to him, “Show us a sign from heaven.
” 2 He answered them, “In the evening you say, ‘The weather will remain clear, because the sky is red’, 3 and in the morning you say, ‘Today a storm will come, because the sky is red and dusty.

’ You can tell the meaning by seeing the signs of the sky, but seeing what is happening in present times, why can't you tell the meaning? 4 The evil and adulterous people of this age look for a sign, but no sign will be given to them except the sign of prophet Jonah.
” And leaving them, he went away.
The disciples reached the other side of the sea, but they had forgotten to take bread.
Jesus said to them regarding their hypocritical teaching, “Look, be cautious of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
” 7 They started discussing among themselves, “We did not bring bread, that is why he speaks like this.

” 8 Knowing this, Jesus said to them, “O you of little faith, why do you discuss among yourselves that we have no bread? 9 Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for those five thousand, nor how many baskets you picked up? 10 And the seven loaves for those four thousand, nor how many baskets you picked up? 11 Why do you not understand that I did not speak to you concerning bread, but that you should be cautious of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
” 12 Then they understood that he had told them to be cautious not of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, and began asking his disciples, “What do people say about me, the Son of Man?” 14 They said, “Some say John the Baptist, and some Elijah, and some Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
” 15 He said to them, “But what do you say about me?” 16 Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
” 17 Jesus answered him, “O Simon, son of Jonah, you are blessed; because flesh and blood did not, but my Father who is in heaven, has revealed this thing to you.
And I also say to you that you are Peter, and I will build my church on this rock, and the gates of the underworld will not prevail against it.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; whatever you bind on earth, it will be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth, it will be loosed in heaven.
” 20 Then he warned the disciples not to tell anyone that I am the Christ.

From that time Jesus began telling his disciples, “It is necessary that I go to Jerusalem and suffer much pain at the hands of Jewish leaders, chief priests, and scribes; and be killed; and rise on the third day.
” 22 Upon this, Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, “O Lord, may God not do this! This will never happen to you.
” 23 He turned and said to Peter, “O Satan, get away from before me! You are a cause of stumbling for me; because you do not set your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.
” 24 Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to become my disciple, let him not fulfill his own will, but pick up the cross of his sufferings and follow behind me.
Because whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

If a man gains the whole world, and suffers the loss of his life, then what benefit will he have? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life? 27 I, the Son of Man, will come in the glory of my Father with my angels, and at that time ‘I will give reward to everyone according to his deeds.
’ 28 “I tell you truly, among those standing here there are some such that until they see me, the Son of Man, coming in his kingdom, until then death will not even touch them.
” After six days Jesus took Peter and James and his brother John along, and took them alone to a high mountain.
There before them a change took place in his appearance, and his face shone like the sun and his clothes became white like light.
And Moses the prophet and Elijah were seen talking with him.
Upon this, Peter said to Jesus, “O Lord, our staying here is good.
If it is your will, I will make three shelters here: one for you, one for Moses the prophet, one for Elijah the prophet.
” 5 He was just speaking when a shining cloud covered them, and from that cloud came out this voice, “This is my beloved son, with whom I am pleased: listen to him.
” 6 disciples Hearing this, the disciples fell on their faces and became very afraid.
Jesus came near and touched them, and said, “Get up, do not be afraid.
” 8 Then they raised their eyes and saw no one except Jesus.
When they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus gave them this command, “Until I, the Son of Man, am raised alive from among the dead, until then do not tell anyone whatever you have seen.
” 10 At this his disciples asked him, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah's coming first is necessary?
” 11 He answered, “Elijah will surely come, and everything will be restored.
But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and people did not recognize him, but did with him whatever they wished.
In this way, I, the Son of Man, will also suffer pain at their hands.
” 13 Then the disciples understood that he spoke to us about John the Baptist.

When they reached near the crowd, a man came near him, and kneeling down began to say, 15 “O Lord, have mercy on my son! Because he gets seizures, and he suffers a lot; and falls again and again into fire and again and again into water.
And I brought him to your disciples, but they could not cure him.
” 17 Jesus answered, “O unbelieving and stubborn people, how long will I stay with you? How long will I endure you? Bring him here to me.
” 18 Then Jesus rebuked the evil spirit, it came out of him and the boy was cured at that very moment.

Then the disciples came near Jesus in private and said, “Why could we not drive it out?” 20 He said to them, “Because of the lack of your faith, because I tell you truly, if your faith is even equal to a mustard seed, then you will be able to say to this mountain, ‘Move from here and go there’, then it will go, and nothing will be impossible for you.
” 21 (But this kind does not come out without prayer and fasting.
) 22 When they were in the region of Galilee, Jesus said to them, “I, the Son of Man, will be handed over into the hands of men.
They will kill me, and on the third day I will become alive.
” At this they became very sad.
When they reached Capernaum, the temple tax collectors came near Peter and asked, “Does your teacher not pay the temple tax?” 25 He said, “Yes, he pays.

When he came home, Jesus spoke to him first before he could ask, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect duty or taxes? From their own sons or from strangers?” Peter said to him, “From strangers.”
Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are exempt.

However, so that we do not offend them, go to the lake, throw in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; when you open its mouth, you will find a coin (worth four days' wages). Take that and give it to them for me and for you.”

At that hour the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” Then he called a child to him, stood him in the midst of them, and said, “Truly I tell you, unless you change and become humble like children, you can never enter the kingdom of heaven.
Whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.
“But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to sin, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the deep sea.
Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For stumbling blocks are bound to come, but woe to that person through whom the stumbling block comes!
If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life maimed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter eternal life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I tell you that in heaven their angels always stand in the presence of my heavenly Father.
(For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.

) What do you think about this? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine, go into the mountains, and search for the one that went astray? And if he happens to find it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
In the same way, it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that even one of these little ones should perish.
“If your fellow believer sins against you, go and point out his fault just between the two of you. If he listens to you and repents, you have won your brother over.
But if he will not listen, take one or two others along with you, so that according to the law of the prophet Moses, 'every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.'
If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church; and if he refuses to listen even to the church, treat him as a Gentile and a tax collector.
“Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
“Again I tell you, if two of you on earth agree about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three gather in my name, there am I in the midst of them.”

Then Peter came to him and said, “Lord, if my brother keeps sinning against me, how many times should I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I do not say to you seven times, but up to seventy times seven times.
“Therefore, the kingdom of heaven may be compared to this illustration: a king wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
When he began the settlement, a man was brought before him who owed him ten thousand talents.
Since he had no way to pay, his master ordered that he, his wife, his children, and all that he owned be sold to pay the debt.
“At this, the servant fell at his feet and said to him, 'O king, be patient with me, and I will pay back everything.'
At this, the king took pity on that servant, released him, and forgave his debt.
“But when that servant went out, he met one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii (100 days' wages); he grabbed him, choked him, and said, 'Pay back what you owe me!'
“At this, his fellow servant fell at his feet and begged him, 'Be patient with me, and I will pay back everything.'
He refused, but went and threw him into prison until he should pay back the debt.
When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were very distressed and went and reported the whole matter to their king.
“Then the king called him in and said to him, 'You wicked servant, I cancelled all that debt of yours because you begged me.
Shouldn't you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?' And in anger, his master handed him over to the jailers to be punished until he should pay back all his debt.
“This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”
When Jesus had finished saying these things, he left the region of Galilee and came to the region of Judea on the other side of the Jordan River.
Then large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.

Then Pharisees came to test him, asking, “Is it lawful to divorce one's wife for any reason?” He answered, “Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, 'For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be united with his wife, and the two will become one flesh'? So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore what God has joined together, let no man separate.”

They said to him, “Why then did the prophet Moses command to give a certificate of divorce and send her away?” He said to them, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of the hardness of your hearts, but it was not so from the beginning.
And I tell you, whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”
The disciples said to Jesus, “If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry.”
Jesus said to them, “Not everyone can accept this teaching, but only those to whom it has been given.

For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb; and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.
Let anyone who can accept this accept it.”

6 When Jesus was in the village of Bethany at the house of Simon the leper, 7 a woman came to him with an expensive fragrant oil in a marble vessel, and poured it on his head as he was sitting down to eat food.

Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, this deed of hers will also be mentioned in memory of her."

14 Then Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve disciples, went to the chief priests and said, 15 "If I hand Jesus over into your hands, what will you give me?" They weighed out thirty silver coins and gave them to him.
And from that time on he began looking for an opportunity to betray Jesus.

On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?" 18 Jesus said, "Go to a certain person in the city and tell him, 'The Teacher says that my time is near.
I will celebrate the Passover festival at your place with my disciples.'"
19 Finally, the disciples obeyed Jesus' command and prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, Jesus sat down to eat food with the twelve disciples.
While they were eating, Jesus said, "Truly I tell you that one of you will betray me and hand me over."
22 At this, the disciples became very sad, and each one began asking him, "Lord, is it me?" 23 Jesus answered, "The one who put his hand into the dish with me, he will betray me.
I, the Son of Man, indeed go as it is written about me; but woe to that man through whom I, the Son of Man, am betrayed: it would have been better for that man if he had not been born."
25 Then Judas, who betrayed Jesus, said, "Lord, is it me?" Jesus said to him, "You have said it."
26 While they were eating the Passover meal, Jesus took bread, asked for a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples saying, "Take, eat; this is my body."
27 Then Jesus took his cup, thanked God, and gave it to them saying, "All of you drink from this, 28 for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

30 Then, after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

” 32 “But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
” 33 At this, Peter said to him, “Even if everyone falls away, I will never leave you.”
” 34 Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
” 35 Peter said to him, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you.”
” All the other disciples said the same thing as well.
Then Jesus came with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane and said to his disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
” 37 He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and troubled.
Then he said to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, even to the point of death.

” 42 He went away a second time and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass away unless I drink it, your will be done.”
” 43 Again he came and found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy with sleep.
Leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go; look, my betrayer is near!
” 47 While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve disciples, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and the elders of the Jews.
Now the betrayer, Judas, had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man; arrest him.”
” 49 And immediately he came up to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him warmly.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you came for.”
” Then they came up, laid hands on Jesus, and arrested him.
And behold, one of those who were with Jesus reached out his hand, drew his sword, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its place, for all who draw the sword will perish by the sword.

Do you not know that I can pray to my Father, and he will at once put more than twelve legions of angels at my disposal? 54 But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?” 55 At that hour Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to capture me as against a robber? Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest me.
But all this has taken place so that the writings of the prophets may be fulfilled.”
” Then all the disciples deserted him and fled.
Those who had arrested Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.
Peter followed him at a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and went inside and sat with the guards to see the outcome.
Now the chief priests and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus to put him to death, 60 but they found none, even though many false witnesses came forward.
Finally two came forward 61 and said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
” 62 Then the high priest stood up and said to Jesus, “Have you no answer to give? What is this testimony that these men are bringing against you?” 63 But Jesus remained silent.
Then the high priest said to him, “I adjure you by the living God: Tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
” 64 Jesus said to him, “You have said it yourself; nevertheless I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Almighty and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

” 65 Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has blasphemed God! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, you have just heard this blasphemy! 66 What do you think?” They answered, “He deserves death.”

” 67 Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists; others slapped him and said, 68 “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is the one who struck you?” 69 Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, “You also were with Jesus the Galilean.”
” 70 But he denied it before them all, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.”
” 71 When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to the people there, “This man was also with Jesus of Nazareth.”
” 72 He denied it again with an oath: “I do not know the man!”
” 73 A little later, the people standing there came up to Peter and said to him, “Surely you too are one of them, for your accent gives you away.”
” 74 Then he began to call down curses and swear to them, “I do not know the man!”
” Immediately a rooster crowed.
Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
” And he went outside and wept bitterly.
Early in the morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the Jews took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
They bound Jesus, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate the governor.

When Judas, his betrayer, saw that Jesus was condemned to death, he felt remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, 4 saying, “I have sinned by betraying an innocent man to death.”
” They said, “What is that to us? That is your responsibility.”
” 5 So Judas threw the coins into the temple court and left, and went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the coins and said, “Our law does not permit us to put these coins into the temple treasury, because it is blood money.”
” 7 So after conferring together, they used the coins to buy the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners.
For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

Then was fulfilled what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet: “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on him by the children of Israel, 10 and they used them to buy the potter's field, as the Lord directed me.”
” 11 Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You say so yourself.”
” 12 When he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he gave no answer.
Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how many things they are testifying against you?” 14 But he gave him no answer, not even to a single charge, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
Now it was the governor's custom at the feast to release for the crowd any one prisoner whom they wanted.
At that time they had a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.
So when they had gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release for you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
” 18 For he knew that it was out of envy that they had handed him over.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent word to him, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered a great deal today in a dream because of him.”
” 20 But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and have Jesus executed.
The governor asked them, “Which of the two do you want me to release for you?” They said, “Barabbas!”

” 22 Pilate said to them, “Then what shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” They all said to him, “Let him be crucified!” 23 The governor said, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they kept shouting all the louder, “Let him be crucified!”

” 24 When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but rather that a riot was starting, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; see to it yourselves!”
” 25 All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!” 26 Then he released Barabbas for them, and after having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.

Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the governor's headquarters and gathered the whole battalion around him, 28 and stripping off his clothes, put a scarlet robe on him, 29 and twisting together a crown of thorns, set it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand; and kneeling down before him, they mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” 30 They spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on his head.
When they had mocked him, they took off the robe, put his own clothes back on him, and led him away to crucify him.
As they were going out, they met a Cyrenian man named Simon.
They forced him to carry his cross.
They came to a place called “The Skull” (which in the Hebrew language is called “Golgotha”).
They gave him wine mixed with gall to drink, but after tasting it, he refused to drink it.
When they had crucified him, they divided his clothes by casting lots, 36 and sitting down there, they kept watch over him.
And above his head they posted the charge against him, which read, “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
” 38 Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.

Those who passed by hurled insults at him, shaking their heads 40 and saying, “You who are going to destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
” 41 In the same way the chief priests, along with the scribes and elders, mocked him, saying, 42 “He saved others, but he cannot save himself!
He is the King of Israel!
Let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him.
He trusts in God; let God deliver him now if He wants him, for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
” 44 In the same way, the robbers who were crucified with him also insulted him.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness came over all that land.

About the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” 47 When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”
” 48 Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, soaked it in sour wine, put it on a reed, and offered it to him to drink.
The rest said, “Wait, let us see if Elijah comes to save him.”
” 50 Then Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and yielded up his spirit.

And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, the earth shook, the rocks were split, 52 the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy people who had fallen asleep were raised, 53 and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
Now when the centurion and those who were with him keeping watch over Jesus saw the earthquake and the things that happened, they were terrified and said, “Truly this was the Son of God!”
” 55 Many women were there watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
When it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who was himself a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Then Pilate ordered the body of Jesus to be given to him.

Joseph took the body of Jesus, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, 60 and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut out in the rock; then he rolled a large stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there, opposite the tomb.

The next day was the Sabbath; on that day the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate and said, 63 “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was still alive, he said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’
’ 64 Therefore, give orders that the tomb be made secure until the third day, lest his disciples come and steal his body away and say to the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’
’ Then the last deception will be worse than the first.”

” (The first deception being that he calls himself the Son of God, and the second that he will now rise from the dead on the third day.) 65 “Pilate said to them, ‘You have a guard of soldiers; go, make the tomb as secure as you know how.’”
So they went with the guard and secured the tomb by sealing the stone.
After the Sabbath, on the first day of the week, early in the morning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And look, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, came near, rolled away the stone, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothes were as white as snow.
Due to his fear, the guards trembled and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus who was crucified."
He is not here, but has risen just as he said.

Come, see the place where the Lord was laid, and go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead and is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see him! Behold, I have told you."
So they left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy and ran to tell his disciples.
Then Jesus met them.
And said, "Greetings!"
They came up and took hold of his feet and worshipped him.
Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid; go and tell my disciples to go to Galilee, there they will see me."
While they were on their way to give this news to the disciples,
some of the guards who were watching the tomb came into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.

Then they gathered with the Jewish leaders, consulted together, gave the soldiers a large sum of money, and instructed them, "Say that while we were asleep at night, his disciples came and stole his body."
If word of your sleeping reaches the governor's ears, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble."
So they took the money and did as they were instructed.
This story is still believed among the Jewish people today.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
When they saw him, they worshipped him, but some doubted that Jesus had risen.
Jesus came near them and said, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me."

Therefore, go and make disciples of all nations; baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you: and behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the world."
The Gospel according to Mark begins with these words, "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God."
In this, Jesus is portrayed as a man who works with authority.
His authority is seen in his teachings, over evil spirits, in his authority, and in the forgiving of people's sins.
In this, Jesus calls himself the "Son of Man."
He came to give his life to redeem people from their sins.
Mark emphasizes not the words and teachings of Jesus, but his actions.
Therefore, he presents his story in a direct, simple, and effective manner.
After a clear account regarding John the Baptist, the baptism of Jesus, and his testing, the author begins to mention the works of Jesus' healing, teaching, and service.
As time passed, Jesus' disciples understood him better, but Jesus' opponents became more hostile.
The final part presents the events of the last week of Jesus' earthly life.
Among which the most important are his crucifixion and his resurrection.
This Gospel is about Jesus Christ.
Who is the Son of God.
And its beginning happened like this, as it is written in the book of the prophet Isaiah that God said to his Son: "Behold, I send my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare the people for you."
A voice of one crying out in the wilderness is heard: Prepare yourselves for the arrival of the Lord.
That messenger was John, who said in the wilderness, "Stop sinning and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins."
All the people of the Judean province and all the residents of the city of Jerusalem went out to him, confessed their sins, and were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
John wore clothes made of camel's hair, had a leather belt around his waist, and ate locusts and honey.
And he preached, "After me comes one who is more powerful than I; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the straps of his sandals."
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
The baptism and testing of Jesus (Matthew 3:13-4:11; Luke 3:21-22; 4:1-13) 9 In those days, Jesus came from the city of Nazareth in the Galilee province and was baptized by John in the Jordan River.
And just as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens opening and the Holy Spirit descending upon him like a dove.
And God spoke from heaven, "You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
Then the Holy Spirit sent him out into the wilderness.
For forty days in the wilderness, Satan tempted him, and he remained with the animals in the wilderness, and the angels were serving him.

The beginning of Jesus' service (Matthew 4:12-17; Luke 4:14-15) 14 After some time had passed since John was arrested, Jesus came into the Galilee province and preached the gospel of the Kingdom of God, and said, "The time is fulfilled, and the Kingdom of God is near; stop sinning and believe in the gospel of God."

The calling of the fishermen (Matthew 4:18-22; Luke 5:1-11) 16 As he was passing by the Sea of Galilee in the Galilee province, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting nets into the sea; because they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, "Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men so that they become my disciples."
They immediately left their nets and followed him to become his disciples.
Walking a little further, he saw James the son of Zebedee and his brother John, mending their nets in the boat.
He called them immediately; and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed him to become his disciples.
Healing a man possessed by an evil spirit (Luke 4:31-37) 21 When Jesus and his disciples arrived at the city of Capernaum, on the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue and began to teach.
And the people were amazed at his teaching; because he did not teach them like the scribes, but with authority.
At that very moment, there was a man in their synagogue who was possessed by an evil spirit.

He cried out, "O Jesus of Nazareth, what do we have to do with you? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are! You are the holy Messiah sent from God!" 25 Jesus rebuked him and said, "Be silent, and come out of this man."
Then the evil spirit shrieked with a loud voice and came out of him.
At this, all the people were astonished and started arguing among themselves, "What is this? This is a new teaching! He commands even the evil spirits with authority, and they obey him!"
And his fame immediately spread everywhere throughout the whole Galilee province.
Healing many sick people (Matthew 8:14-17; Luke 4:38-41) 29 Jesus and all his disciples immediately left the synagogue and came to the house of Simon and Andrew, along with James and John.
Simon's mother-in-law was down with a fever, and his disciples told Jesus about her immediately.
Then Jesus went near, took her hand, and raised her up; her fever left her, and she began to serve them.
At evening, when the sun had set, the people brought all the sick and those who were possessed by evil spirits to Jesus.
And the whole city was gathered at the door.

He healed many who were suffering from various kinds of diseases, cast out many evil spirits, and did not allow the evil spirits to speak, because they recognized him, that Jesus was the Messiah sent from God.
Jesus praying alone (Luke 4:42-44) 35 Early the next day before daybreak, Jesus got up from Simon's house, went out to a deserted place, and began to pray there.
Then Simon and his companions went in search of him.
When they found him, they said, "All the people of the city are looking for you."
He said to them, "Come; let us go to the other surrounding villages, so that I may preach there as well, because that is why I have come."
And he went throughout all the Galilee province, preaching in their synagogues and casting out evil spirits.
Healing a leper (Matthew 8:1-4; Luke 5:12-16) 40 A leper came to him, begged him, knelt before him, and said, "If you want, you can make me well."
He had compassion on him, reached out his hand, touched him, and said, "I want to, be healed from this disease."
And immediately his leprosy left him, and he was healed.

Then he warned him and sent him away, 44 and said to him, "Listen, do not tell anything to anyone, but go and show yourself to the priest, and offer the sacrifice that Moses the prophet prescribed in the Holy Scriptures for your healing from leprosy, as a testimony to the people that you have been healed."
But he went out and began to preach and spread the word so much that Jesus could no longer go openly into the city, but stayed outside in lonely places, and people from all around kept coming to him.
A few days later, Jesus came to the city of Capernaum again, and the people heard that he was at home.
Then so many people gathered that there was no room left near the door, and he was teaching them the Word of God.
And four men brought a paralytic lying on a mat to him.
But when they could not reach him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof under which Jesus was; then they lowered the mat on which the paralytic was lying.
Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, "Son, your sins are forgiven."

6 Then many scribes who were sitting there began to think in their hearts, 7 "Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming God! Who can forgive sins except God?" 8 Jesus immediately knew in his heart why they were thinking like this? And said to them, "Why are you thinking this in your hearts? 9 Which is easier? To say to the paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up, pick up your mat, and walk'? 10 But so that you may know that I, the Son of Man, have authority on earth to forgive sins too."
He said to the paralytic, 11 "I say to you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home."
He got up, immediately picked up his mat, and went out in front of them; at this everyone was amazed and began to praise God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this before."
The calling of Levi (Matthew 9:9-13; Luke 5:27-32) 13 Jesus went out again by the Sea of Galilee, and all the crowds came to him, and he began to teach them.
As he was passing, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, whose name was Matthew, sitting at the tax office and said to him, "Follow me to become my disciple."
And he got up and followed him.

When he was sitting at Matthew's house for a meal, many tax collectors and those whom the people called sinners were sitting to eat with Jesus and his disciples; because there were many of them, and they had followed him.
The scribes and Pharisees, seeing that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, "Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and those whom people call sinners?"
17 Jesus heard this and said to them, "The healthy do not need a doctor, but the sick do: I have not come to call those who call themselves righteous, but those who call themselves sinners."

The question of fasting (Matthew 9:14-17; Luke 5:33-39) 18 John's disciples and the Pharisees used to fast, so they came and said to him, "Why do John's disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?" 19 Jesus said to them, "As long as the bridegroom is with the wedding guests, can they fast? In the end, as long as the bridegroom is with them, they cannot fast."
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them; in that day they will fast.
“No one puts a patch of new cloth on old clothes, otherwise the patch will tear away from it, meaning the new from the old, and it will tear even more than before.

No one puts new grape juice into old wineskins, otherwise the grape juice will burst the wineskins, and both the grape juice and the wineskins will be destroyed, but new grape juice is to be put into new wineskins."

The Lord of the Sabbath (Matthew 12:1-8; Luke 6:1-5) 23 It happened that on the Sabbath, Jesus was passing through the fields with his disciples, and as they walked, his disciples began to pick heads of wheat.
So the Pharisees said to him, "Look, why do they do that on the Sabbath? Which is against the rules and regulations."

25 Jesus said to them, "Have you not read in the Holy Scriptures what our ancestor David did when he was in need, and when he and his companions were hungry? 26 How, in the time of Abiathar the high priest, he went into the house of God and ate the bread of the offering, which it is not right for anyone to eat except the priests, and he even gave some to his companions?" 27 Then he said to them, "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath."
Therefore, I am the Lord even of the Sabbath."

Jesus went into the synagogue again on the Sabbath; there was a man there whose hand was withered, 2 and the Pharisees were watching Jesus to see if he would heal him on the Sabbath, so they could accuse him.
He said to the man with the withered hand, "Stand up in the middle." 4 And he said to them, "Is it right on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to kill?" But they remained silent.
Then, looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he said to the man, 'Stretch out your hand.'
He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
Then the Pharisees went out and immediately began to consult with the supporters of King Herod as to how they might destroy him.

Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea of Galilee, and a great multitude from Galilee followed him; and a great multitude from Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, from beyond the Jordan, and from around Tyre and Sidon, hearing what great things he was doing, came to see him.
Jesus said to his disciples, 'Keep a small boat ready for me because of the crowd, so that they cannot press upon me.'
For he had healed many, so that as many as were sick pressed upon him to touch him.
And whenever unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and shouted, saying, 'You are the Son of God.'
And he warned the unclean spirits not to tell anyone who he was.
Then Jesus went up on the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted; and they came to him.
And he appointed twelve disciples to be with him, to send them out to preach, and to have the authority to cast out unclean spirits.
These are the twelve disciples: Simon, whom he named Peter, and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, whom he named Boanerges, which means 'Sons of Thunder.'
And Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
Then Jesus came home; and the crowd gathered again, so that Jesus and his disciples could not even eat.

When his relatives heard this, they went out to take him home; for they were saying, 'He is out of his mind.' The scribes who came from Jerusalem were also saying, 'He is possessed by Satan,' and, 'He casts out demons by the help of Satan, the ruler of the demons.'

So Jesus called them to him and began speaking to them in parables, 'How can Satan cast out demons? If a kingdom is divided against itself, how can that kingdom stand? And if a house is divided against itself, how will that house be able to stand? So if Satan rises up against himself and is divided, how can he remain? He is coming to an end.'
'No one can enter a strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man; then he will plunder his house.'
'I tell you truly, all sins and evil that people commit will be forgiven, but whoever commits evil against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven: he will be guilty of an eternal sin.'
Because they were saying that he had an unclean spirit.
Then Jesus' mother and his brothers arrived, and standing outside, they sent for him.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him, 'Look, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.'
Jesus answered them, 'Who are my mother and my brothers?' And looking at those sitting around him, he said, 'Behold, my mother and my brothers are these.'
'For whoever does the will of God, he is my brother, my sister, and my mother.'
Jesus began to teach again by the sea of Galilee, and such a large crowd gathered to him that he got into a boat and sat in it, and all the crowd remained standing on the shore of the sea.
He began to teach them many things in parables, and in his teaching, he said to them, 'Listen! A farmer went out to sow seed.'
As he sowed, some fell by the wayside, and the birds came and ate it up.
Some fell on rocky ground where it did not get much soil, and because it did not find deep soil, it grew briefly, and when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
Some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them, and they produced no fruit.
But some fell on good soil, and it grew and increased and produced fruit; and it brought forth thirty-fold, sixty-fold, and some a hundred-fold.
Then he said, 'He who has ears to hear, let him listen carefully.'
When Jesus was alone, his companions along with the twelve disciples asked him about these parables.
He said to them, 'To you has been given the mystery of the kingdom of God, but for those outside, everything is in parables.'
'So that they may look and look, but not see, and listen and listen, but not understand; lest they should stop sinning and be forgiven.'
Then Jesus said to them, 'Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the other parables? The farmer who sows is like the one who sows the word.'
The seeds that fell by the wayside are like those who hear the word, but as soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
In the same way, those who received the seed on rocky ground are those who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy.
But because they have no root in themselves, they last only for a short time; then when trouble or persecution arises because of the word, they stumble immediately.

Those who received the seed among thorns are those who heard the word, but the worries of the world, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desires for other things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And those who received seed on good soil are those who hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit: some thirty, some sixty, and some a hundred-fold.

Jesus gave them another parable, 'Do you light a lamp to put it under a vessel or a bed? Or do you put it on a stand? There is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing is secret that will not be brought to light.'
If anyone has ears to hear, let him listen carefully.
Then he said to them, 'Pay close attention to what you hear.'
With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you.
And more will be given to you.
For to him who has, more will be given, and from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away.

Then Jesus gave them another parable, 'The kingdom of God is as if a man scatters seed upon the ground, and goes to bed at night and wakes up in the morning, and the seed grows and increases without him knowing how.'
The earth produces fruit by itself: first the blade, then the head, and then the full grain in the head.
But when the grain is ripe, he puts in the sickle, because the time of harvest has come.

Then Jesus gave them another parable, 'To what can we compare the kingdom of God, or with what parable can we explain it? It is like a mustard seed; when it is sown in the ground, it is the smallest of all the seeds on earth, but when it is sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all garden herbs, and puts out such large branches that the birds of the air can nest in its shade.'
