And they kept watching him and sent spies who pretended to be righteous, in order to catch him in something he said, so that they could hand him over to the governor's power and authority.
They asked him, 'Teacher, we know that you speak and teach correctly, and you show no partiality, but teach the way of God according to truth.'
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?' 23 He discerned their craftiness and said to them, 24 'Show me a denarius (a day's wage).
Whose likeness and name is on this?' They said, 'Caesar's.'
” 25 He said to them, 'Then give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.'
” 26 They could not catch him in his words before the people, but were amazed at his answer and remained silent.
Resurrection and Marriage 27 Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and asked,
Luke 20:27-47 28 'Teacher, Moses the prophet wrote for us: If a man's brother dies leaving a wife but no children, his brother must marry the wife and produce descendants for his brother.'
Then the second and the third one also married that woman.
In this way, all seven died childless.
In the end, that woman also died.
In the end, when they rise again, whose wife will she be, because she was the wife of all seven?
Jesus said to them, 'The people of this age marry, but those who are considered worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead, they do not marry.'
They will not die anymore, because they will be like angels, and being children of the resurrection, they will also be children of God.
But that the dead rise, even Moses showed in the story of the bush, where he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'
God is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for to Him, all are alive.
Then, hearing this, some of the scribes said, 'O Teacher, you have spoken well.'
And they dared not ask him anything else.

Whose son is the Christ? Then he asked them, 'How do they say that the Christ is the son of David? David himself says in the book of Psalms: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.'

David calls him Lord, so how is he his son? Warning against scribes: As all were listening, he said to his disciples, 'Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, and the best seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at feasts.'
They devour widows' houses and for a show make long prayers: they will receive greater punishment.
Then looking up, he saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
He also saw a poor widow putting two copper coins (which are equal to a penny) into it.
Then he said, 'Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.'
Because all of them contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty has put in all that she had to live on.

Prophecy of the destruction of the temple: As some were speaking about the temple, how it was adorned with beautiful stones and gifts, he said, 'The days will come when all these things you see, there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down.'

Tribulation and distress: They asked him, 'Teacher, when will this be? And what will be the sign when these things are about to happen?' He said, 'Watch out that you are not deceived, because many will come in my name, saying, I am he, and the time is near.'
Do not go after them.
When you hear of wars and tumults, do not be afraid, for these things must happen first, but the end will not be then.

Then he said to them, 'Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and pestilences, and there will be terrifying events and great signs from heaven.'
But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, and deliver you up to synagogues, and put you in prisons, and bring you before kings and governors.
But this will be an opportunity for you to give testimony.
Therefore, resolve in your own hearts not to worry about what answer you will give beforehand.
Because I will give you such speech and wisdom that all your adversaries will not be able to oppose or refute.
You will be betrayed even by your parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and some of you they will have put to death.
All men will hate you because of my name.
But not a hair of your head will perish.
By your endurance you will save your lives.
Prophecy of the destruction of Jerusalem: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and those who are inside the city of Jerusalem depart, and let not those who are in the country enter it.
For these will be days of vengeance, in which all that is written will be fulfilled.
In those days, those who are pregnant and nursing mothers will be in trouble! For there will be great distress in the land and wrath upon this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and will be led captive among all nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the time of the Gentiles is fulfilled.
The return of the Son of Man: There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on the earth distress among nations, for they will be perplexed by the roaring of the sea and the waves.
Men will faint from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with power and great glory.
When these things begin to take place, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.
Parable of the fig tree: Jesus told them a parable, 'Look at the fig tree and all the trees.'
As soon as they sprout leaves, you yourselves know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
I tell you the truth, this generation will not pass away until all these things have taken place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
Watch: Be careful, lest your hearts be weighed down with debauchery, drunkenness, and the worries of this life, and that day comes on you suddenly like a trap.
For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of the whole earth.
Therefore, stay awake and pray at all times so that you may be able to escape all these things that are about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
He was teaching in the temple during the day, and at night he would go out and stay on the mount called Olivet, and early in the morning all the people would come to him in the temple to hear him.
The feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was near.
And the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way.
How they might kill Jesus, but they feared the people.
Betrayal of Judas: Then Satan entered Judas, who was called Iscariot and was counted among the twelve disciples.
He went and conferred with the chief priests and captains of the guard on how he might betray Jesus to them.
They were glad and promised to give him money.
He agreed and began to look for an opportunity to betray him to them when no crowd was present.
The last Passover meal with the disciples: Then the day of Unleavened Bread arrived, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, 'Go and prepare the Passover for us to eat.'

They asked Jesus, 'Where do you want us to prepare it?' Jesus said to the disciples, 'Look, when you enter the city, a man carrying a water jar will meet you; follow him into the house he enters, and say to the master of the house, The Teacher asks you, where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples? He will show you a large furnished upper room, make preparations there.'
They went and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
The Lord's Supper: When the hour came, Jesus sat down to eat with the apostles.
And he said to them, 'I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.'
For I tell you the truth, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
Then he took the cup of grape juice, gave thanks to God, and said, 'Take this and divide it among yourselves.'
For I tell you, from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.
Then Jesus took bread and gave thanks to God and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, 'This is my body which is given for you: do this in remembrance of me.'
In the same way, he also gave the cup after supper, saying, 'This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.'
But look, the one who betrays me is with me at this table.

For the Son of Man goes as it has been determined for me, just as it has been ordained, but woe to that man by whom I am betrayed! Then they began to ask among themselves which of them it was who would do this.
Who is the greatest? Disputes: A dispute also arose among them as to who was considered the greatest among them.
Jesus said to them, 'The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.'
But you are not to be like that; instead, the one who is greatest among you should become like the youngest, and the leader like the one who serves.
For who is the greater, the one who sits at the table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.

You are those who have remained with me in my trials, and just as my Father has assigned a kingdom to me, so I assign to you, so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom and sit on thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
Prophecy of Peter's denial: 'Simon, Simon! Look, Satan has asked for permission from God to test you as a farmer separates wheat from chaff.'
But I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail, and when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.
Peter said to him, 'Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison, and even to death.'
He said, 'Peter, I tell you truly, before the rooster crows today, you will deny three times that you know me.'
Money bag, bag, and sword: Then Jesus said to the disciples, 'When I sent you out to preach without a money bag, or bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?' They said, 'Nothing at all.'
He said to the disciples, 'But now, let him who has a money bag take it, and likewise, let him who has no sword sell his clothes and buy one.'
For I tell you, this which is written in the Holy Scriptures, 'He was counted with the transgressors,' must be fulfilled in me, for everything written about me must be fulfilled.
The disciples said, 'Lord, here are two swords.'
Jesus said to them, 'That is enough.'
Jesus' prayer on the Mount of Olives: Then Jesus went out as was his custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed him.
When he reached the place, he said to the disciples, 'Pray that you may not fall into temptation.'
And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw and knelt down and prayed, 'Father, if you are willing, take this cup of suffering away from me, nevertheless, not my will but yours be done.'
Then an angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him.
Being in great agony, he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat was like great drops of blood falling to the ground.
Then he rose from prayer and came to his disciples and found them sleeping for sorrow.
And said to them, 'Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray that you may not fall into temptation.'
Jesus' arrest by betrayal: Jesus was still speaking when a crowd arrived, and one of the twelve disciples named Judas was leading them.
He approached Jesus to kiss him.

Jesus said to him, 'Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?' His followers, when they saw what was going to happen, said, 'Lord, should we strike with the sword?' And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
On this, Jesus said, 'Stop, no more of this.'
And he touched his ear and healed him.

Then Jesus said to the chief priests, the captains of the temple guard, and the Jewish leaders who had come against him, 'Have you come out with swords and clubs as if against a robber? When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not lay a hand on me, but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.'
Peter's denial: Then they seized Jesus and led him away, bringing him into the high priest's house, while Peter followed at a distance.
And when they had kindled a fire in the courtyard and sat down together, Peter also sat among them.
A servant girl, seeing him sitting in the light of the fire and looking at him, said, 'This man was also with him.'
But Peter denied it, saying, 'Woman, I do not know him.'
A little later, someone else saw Peter and said, 'You also are one of them.'
He said, 'Oh brother, I am not that one.'
About an hour later, another person said with firm conviction, 'Certainly, this man was also with him, because he is a Galilean.'

Peter said, 'Oh brother, I don't know what you are saying!' He was still saying this when the rooster crowed. Then the Lord turned and looked at Peter, and Peter remembered the word of the Lord which He had told him: 'Before the rooster crows today, you will deny me three times.'
And he went outside and wept bitterly.

Insult to Jesus: The men who had arrested Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him, and having blindfolded Him, asked Him, 'Prophesy and tell us who hit you!' And they said many blasphemous things against Him.

Jesus before the Council: When the day broke, the Jewish leaders, chief priests, and scribes gathered together, brought Him into their Great Council, and asked, 'If you are the Messiah, tell us!' He said to them, 'If I tell you, you will not believe, and if I ask, you will not answer.'
But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the Almighty God.
To this, everyone asked, 'So, are you the Son of God?' Jesus said to them, 'You yourselves are saying it, because I am.'
Then they said, 'Now what need do we have for witnesses, because we have heard it ourselves from his own mouth.'
Then the whole assembly got up and took Jesus to the governor, Pilate.
Luke 23:1-25: They began to accuse Him, saying, 'We have heard this man inciting the people, forbidding them to pay taxes to Caesar, and claiming to be Messiah, a king himself.'
Pilate asked Him, 'Are you the King of the Jews?' He replied to him, 'You yourself are saying it.'
Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the people, 'I have found no fault in this man.'
But they persisted even more strongly, saying, 'He is causing riots by teaching people throughout all of Judea, starting from the province of Galilee up to here.'
Hearing this, Pilate asked, 'Is this man a Galilean?' And knowing that he belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, because he was also in Jerusalem at that time.
Jesus before Herod: Herod was very happy to see Jesus, because he had wanted to see Him for a long time, as he had heard about Him and hoped to see some miracle from Him.
He kept asking Him many questions, but He gave him no answer at all.
The chief priests and scribes stood there and kept accusing Him with full intensity.
Then Herod, along with his soldiers, mocked Him by treating Him with contempt and, dressing Him in a flashy robe, sent Him back to Pilate.
That same day, Pilate and Herod became friends; before this, they were enemies of each other.

Death sentence for Jesus by Pilate: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people and said to them, 'You brought this man to me as one who incites the people, and look, I have examined Him in your presence, but I have found no fault in Him regarding the things you accuse Him of. Neither has Herod found Him guilty, because he has sent Him back to us: and look, nothing has been done by Him that makes Him worthy of the death penalty.'
Therefore, I will scourge Him and release Him.
(Pilate was compelled to release one prisoner for them at the time of the festival.)

Then they all shouted together, 'Finish Him off, and release Barabbas for us!' He had been put in jail because of some riot that had occurred in the city and for murder. But Pilate, wishing to release Jesus, tried to persuade the people again. Finally, they shouted, 'Crucify Him, crucify Him!' He said to them for the third time, 'Why, what evil has He done? I have not found any reason in Him that warrants the death penalty.'
In this way, I will scourge Him and release Him.
But they insisted with shouts that He be crucified, and their shouting grew louder.
Finally, Pilate gave the order that it be done according to their request.
He released the man who had been put in jail for riot and murder, the one they asked for, and handed Jesus over according to their will.
Jesus being crucified: As they were taking Jesus away, they grabbed a man named Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, and loaded the cross on him so he could carry it behind Jesus.
Luke 23:26-43: A crowd of people followed Him; among them were many women who were beating their chests and weeping for Him.

Jesus turned towards them and said, 'Oh daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children, because look, the days are coming when people will say, "Blessed are those women who are barren, and the wombs that have not borne children, and the breasts that have not nursed."
'At that time, people will begin to say to the mountains and hills, "Fall on us and cover us."
Because if they do this with green trees, what will not be done with the dry ones?'
They also took two other men who were criminals to be executed along with Jesus.
When they reached the place which is called 'The Skull', or 'Golgotha' in the Hebrew language, they crucified Jesus there, as well as the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.
Then Jesus said, 'Oh Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they are doing.'
And they cast lots and divided His clothes.
The people stood and watched, and the rulers also mocked Him, saying, 'He saved others; if this is God's Messiah and His chosen one, then let Him save himself.'

The soldiers also came near, offered Him vinegar, and mocking Him, said, 'If you are the King of the Jews, then save yourself!' And they also put an accusation above Him: 'This is the King of the Jews.'

The repentant criminal: One of the criminals who were hanged there insulted Him, saying, 'Aren't you the Messiah? Then save yourself and us!' But the other rebuked him and said, 'Don't you fear God? You are also receiving the same punishment. We are getting the punishment according to our deeds, because we are getting the right reward for our actions, but He has done nothing wrong.'
Then he said, 'Oh Jesus, when you come into your kingdom, remember me.'
He said to him, 'I tell you the truth, today you will be with me in Paradise.'
Around noon until three o'clock, darkness covered the whole land,
Luke 23:44-56: And the light of the sun faded, and the curtain of the temple was torn down the middle, and Jesus cried out with a loud voice, 'Oh Father, I commit my spirit into your hands.'
And saying this, He breathed His last.
The centurion, having seen what happened, praised God and said, 'Certainly, this man was righteous.'
And the crowd that had gathered to see this, seeing this event, went back beating their chests in grief.
But all His acquaintances, and the women who had come with Him from the province of Galilee, stood at a distance and watched all this.

The burial of Jesus: There was a man named Joseph, a member of the council of Jewish leaders, who was a good and righteous man; 51 he was not in agreement with the decision of the council or this action.
He was from the town of Arimathea in the province of Judea and was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus, and having taken it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth and placed it in a grave that had been carved out of stone, where no one had ever been laid.
It was the day of preparation, and the Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with Him from the province of Galilee followed and saw the grave, and also how His body was placed.
Then they returned home and prepared spices and perfumes, and they rested on the Sabbath day according to the commandment.
But on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to Jesus' grave with the spices that they had prepared.
Luke 24:1-35: They found the stone rolled away from the grave, but going inside, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
While they were astonished by this, look, two men in shining clothes stood beside them.
As they were afraid and kept their faces bowed to the ground, they said to them, 'Why are you looking for the living among the dead? 6 He is not here, but has risen.'
Remember what He told you while He was in the province of Galilee, 7 that it is necessary that the Son of Man be handed over into the hands of sinners, be crucified, and rise on the third day.
Then they remembered His words,
And returning from the grave, they told all these things to the eleven and to all the others.
Those who said these things to the apostles were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and other women who were with them.
But their words seemed like a story to them, and they did not believe it.
Then Peter ran to the grave, and bowing down, saw the linen wrappings lying there, and went back to his home wondering about what had happened.
Appearance to disciples on the road to Emmaus: That same day, two of the disciples were going to a village named Emmaus, which was about seven miles away from Jerusalem.
They were walking along, discussing all these things that had happened, and as they were talking and questioning each other, Jesus himself came near and began walking with them.
But God had blinded their eyes so that they could not recognize Jesus.
Jesus asked them, 'What is this that you are discussing as you walk?' They stood still, and their faces were very sad.

Hearing this, one of the disciples named Cleopas said, 'It seems you are the only stranger in Jerusalem who doesn't know what has happened in this city in these days?' Jesus asked them, 'What things?' They said to Him, 'About Jesus of Nazareth who was a prophet, who was mighty in work and word before God and all the people.'
And our chief priests and rulers handed Him over to be sentenced to death, and had Him crucified.
But we were hoping that He would redeem Israel from the Roman empire.

Besides all these things, today is the third day since this event happened, 22 and several women among us have also put us in confusion, who went to the grave early this morning, 23 and when they did not find His body, they came back saying that we saw visions of angels, who said that Jesus is alive.
Then several of our companions went to the grave and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see Him.'

Then Jesus said to those two disciples, 'Oh foolish ones and slow of heart to believe in all the things of the prophets! 26 Wasn't it necessary for the Messiah to suffer these things and enter into His glory?' 27 Then starting from Moses the prophet and all the prophets, He explained to them the meaning of the things written about himself in all the Holy Scriptures.
By this time, they reached the village where they were going, and He appeared as if He wanted to go further.
But they urged Him, saying, 'Stay with us, because it is evening and the day has now declined much.'
Then He went inside to stay with them.
When He sat down to eat with them, He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and began giving it to them.
Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized Him, and He vanished from their sight.

They said to each other, 'When He was talking to us on the way and explaining the meaning of the Holy Scripture, didn't our hearts burn within us?' 33 At that very moment, they got up and went to the city of Jerusalem, and found the eleven disciples and their companions gathered together.
They were saying, 'The Lord has truly risen, and has appeared to Simon.'
Then those two disciples also told the details of the event that happened on the road and how they had recognized Messiah Jesus while eating.
Jesus appearing to the disciples: While they were talking about this, He himself stood in their midst and said to them, 'Peace be to you.'
Luke 24:36-53: But they were terrified and afraid, and thought they were seeing a spirit.
Jesus asked them, 'Why are you troubled? And why do doubts arise in your hearts? 39 See my hands and feet that it is I myself.'
Touch me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see I have.
Saying this, He showed them the wounds on His hands and feet.
When they did not believe because of joy and were wondering, Jesus asked them, 'Do you have anything here to eat?' 42 The disciples gave Him a piece of broiled fish.
He took that piece of fish and ate it in front of them.

Then He said to them, 'These are my words which I spoke to you while I was with you, that it is necessary that everything written about me in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the books of psalms be fulfilled.'

Then He opened their minds to understand the Holy Scripture, 46 and said to them, 'It is written in the Holy Scripture that the Messiah will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, 47 and repentance and forgiveness of sins will be preached in His name, starting from Jerusalem to all nations.'
You are witnesses of all these things.
And look, I will send the Holy Spirit on you as my Father has said; until the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you receive power from heaven, stay in this city.
The Ascension of Jesus: Then Jesus led them out to the village of Bethany, and lifting His hands, He blessed them, 51 and while blessing them, He was parted from them and taken up to heaven.
Then they worshiped Him and went back to Jerusalem with great joy, 53 and they were continuously present in the temple praising God.
In the Gospel written by John, Jesus is presented as the eternal Word of God, who took on flesh and dwelt among us.

In this book, it is clearly said that this Gospel was written so that those who read it may believe that Jesus is the promised Savior and Son of God, and that they may have life through faith in Jesus Christ (20:31).

In the introduction, Jesus is shown as the eternal Word of God; after that, in the first part of the Gospel, seven miracles or wonderful deeds are mentioned, through which it is revealed that Jesus is the promised Savior and the Son of God.
The second part is teaching.
In them, it is explained what the meaning of these miracles is.
This part explains how some people believed in Jesus and became his disciples, while others opposed him and refused to believe.
Chapters 13-17 describe the night Jesus was betrayed, his deep fellowship with his disciples, and his detailed words of preparation and encouragement to them on the evening before his crucifixion.
The final chapters describe the arrest and trial of Jesus, his crucifixion, his resurrection, and his appearance to the disciples after he was raised to life.
John emphasizes the gift of eternal life through Christ.
This is a gift that begins now and is received by those who find Jesus as the way, the truth, and the life.
Using ordinary everyday things as symbols to illustrate spiritual truths is a specialty of John, such as water, bread, light, the shepherd and his sheep, and the vine and its fruit.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was with God in the beginning.
Everything in the world was made through him, and without him, nothing was created.
He was the source of life, and that life was the light for humanity.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness could not extinguish it.
A man sent from God came, whose name was John.
He came to testify to the light, so that all people might believe in the light through him.
He was not the light himself, but he came to testify to that light.
The true light that gives the light of knowledge to every person was coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, but the people of the world did not recognize him.
He came to his own Jewish people, and his own people did not accept him.
But to all who did accept him, he gave the right to become children of God.
They were born not naturally through ancestors, nor by human desire, nor by the will of man, but by the will of God.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, full of grace and truth, and we saw his glory, the glory of the Father’s only Son.
John testified about him and cried out, “This is the one I spoke of when I said that the one coming after me is much greater than me because he was before me.”
For from the fullness of his grace and truth, we have all received grace upon grace.
For the law was given through the prophet Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God, but the only Son of God, who is always with the Father, has made him known to us.

The testimony of John the Baptist (Matthew 3:1-12; Mark 1:1-8; Luke 3:1-18) 19 John’s testimony is this: when the Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?” 20 he did not deny it, but confessed, “I am not the Messiah.”
21 Then they asked John, “Then who are you? Are you Elijah the prophet?” He clearly said, “I am not.”
“Are you that Prophet?” He answered, “No.”
22 Then they asked John, “Then who are you? So that we can give an answer to those who sent us.
What do you say about yourself?” 23 He said, “As the prophet Isaiah spoke: ‘I am the voice of one calling out in the wilderness, make straight the path of the Lord.’
24 They were sent by the Pharisees.

They asked him this question, “If you are not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor that Prophet, then why do you baptize?” 26 John answered them, “I baptize you with water, but standing among you is someone you do not know.
That is, the one coming after me, whose shoelaces I am not even worthy to untie.”
28 This happened in Bethany on the other side of the Jordan River, where John used to baptize people.
The Lamb of God 29 The next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, this is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
This is the one I was talking about, a man comes after me who is greater than me, for he was before me.
I did not recognize him myself, but I came baptizing with water for this very reason, so that the people of Israel might know him.”
32 And John gave this testimony: “I saw the Holy Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Jesus the Messiah.
33 I did not recognize him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me, ‘The one on whom you see the Spirit descend and rest is the one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.’
34 “And I have seen, and I testify, that this is the Son of God.”
Jesus’ first disciples 35 The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples, 36 and noticing Jesus as he was passing by, he said, “Look, the Lamb of God.”
37 Immediately those two disciples heard his words and followed Jesus.
Jesus turned around, saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Teacher, where are you staying?” 39 Jesus said to them, “Come, and you will see.”
39 So they saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day.
Because it was about four in the evening.
Of the two who heard John’s words and followed Jesus, one was Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter.
He first found his own brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Christ, that is, the Messiah (the anointed one of God).”
42 Then Andrew brought Simon to Jesus.
Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon, son of John: you will be called Cephas, that is, Peter.”
The calling of Philip and Nathanael 43 The next day Jesus decided to go to the Galilee region.
He found Philip and said, “Follow me.”
44 Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one whom the prophet Moses wrote about in the law and whom the prophets spoke about! He is Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
46 Nathanael asked him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, “Look, this is a true Israelite; there is no deceit in him.”
48 Nathanael asked him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, I saw you while you were under the fig tree.”
49 Nathanael answered him, “Teacher, you are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel.”
50 Jesus answered him, “Because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than this.”
51 Then he said, “I tell you the truth, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
Then, on the third day, there was a wedding in the town of Cana in the Galilee region, and Jesus’ mother was also there.
Jesus and his disciples were also invited to that wedding.
When the grape juice ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no more grape juice left.”
4 Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you telling me this? My time has not yet come.”
5 But his mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
6 According to Jewish tradition, six stone water jars were placed there for purification, in which two or three maunds of water could come.
Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.”
And they filled them to the brim.
Then Jesus said to the servants, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast.”
And they took it.

When the master of the feast tasted the water that had turned into grape juice, and did not know where it had come from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew, the master of the feast called the bridegroom and said, 10 “Everyone serves the best grape juice first, and when people have drunk their fill, then they serve the weaker one, but you have saved the best grape juice until now.”
11 Jesus performed this, his first sign-miracle, in the town of Cana in the Galilee region and revealed his glory, because of which his disciples believed in him.
After this, he, his mother, his brothers, and his disciples went to the city of Capernaum and stayed there for a few days.
The casting out of traders from the temple (Matthew 21:12-13; Mark 11:15-17; Luke 19:45-46) 13 The Jewish festival of Passover was near, and Jesus went to the city of Jerusalem.
He found people selling oxen, sheep, and doves, and money changers (those who exchanged money) sitting in the temple.

Then he made a whip of cords, drove all the sheep and oxen out of the temple, scattered the money of the money changers, and overturned their tables, 16 and said to those selling doves, “Take these things away from here.”
“Do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.”
17 Then his disciples remembered that it was written in the Holy Scripture, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”
18 The Jewish leaders said to Jesus, “What miraculous sign can you show us?” That these things you do, it can be proven that you have the authority for it.
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and I will build it in three days.”
20 The Jewish leaders said, “It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and will you build it in three days?” 21 But Jesus was speaking to them about the temple of his own body.
Eventually, when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed in the scripture that tells about Jesus’ resurrection and the words Jesus had spoken.
Jesus knows the human heart 23 During the days of the Passover festival when Jesus was in the city of Jerusalem, many people believed in him after seeing the signs and miracles he performed.

But Jesus did not trust himself to them, because he knew them all, 25 and he had no need for anyone to come and tell him about humans, because he himself knew what was in the human heart. Among the Pharisees was a man named Nicodemus, who was a leader of the Jews.
He came to Jesus at night and said to him, “Teacher, we know that you have come from God to teach us, because no one can show these signs that you show if God is not with him.”
3 Jesus answered him, “I tell you the truth, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
4 Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time and be born?”
5 Jesus answered, “I tell you the truth, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.”
Because birth in human flesh is only a birth of the flesh, whereas birth from the Spirit is a new birth.
Do not be surprised that I told you it is necessary for you to be born again.
The wind blows wherever it wants, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So is everyone born of the Holy Spirit.”

9 Nicodemus answered him, how can this happen? 10 Hearing this, Jesus answered him, “Being a teacher of the Israelites, do you not understand these things?” 11 I tell you the truth, we speak what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and you do not believe what we say.

When I told you about earthly things and you do not believe, then how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things? 13 And no one has ascended to heaven, only he who descended from heaven, that is, I, the Son of Man.
And just as the prophet Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the wilderness, so it is necessary that I, the Son of Man, also be lifted up.
So that whoever believes in me may have eternal life.
For God so loved the people of the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him will not perish but have eternal life.
For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him.
Whoever believes in the Son of God is not condemned, but whoever does not believe will be judged, because they have not believed in the name of the only Son of God.
And the reason for the judgment is that the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness more than the light because their deeds were evil.
For whoever does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, because their sins will be exposed.
But whoever lives by the truth comes to the light, so that it may be proven that their deeds were done through God.
John’s testimony about Jesus 22 After this, Jesus and his disciples arrived in the region of Judea, and he stayed there with them and began to baptize people.
John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there, and people came and were baptized.
For John had not yet been put in prison.
Then there arose a dispute between some of John's disciples and the Jews about purification.
And they came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, He who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified—behold, He is baptizing, and all are coming to Him!”
John answered and said, “A man can receive nothing unless it has been given to him from heaven.
You yourselves bear me witness, that I said, ‘I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘I have been sent before Him.’
He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore this joy of mine is fulfilled.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
He who comes from above is above all; he who is of the earth is earthly and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.
And what He has seen and heard, that He testifies; and no one receives His testimony.
He who has received His testimony has certified that God is true.
For He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into His hand.
He who believes in the Son has everlasting life; and he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides on him.”
Therefore, when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John—
(though Jesus Himself did not baptize, but His disciples), 3 He left Judea and departed again to Galilee. 4 But He needed to go through Samaria.
So He came to a city of Samaria which is called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
Now Jacob’s well was there.
Jesus therefore, wearied from His journey, sat thus by the well.
It was about the sixth hour.
A woman of Samaria came to draw water.
Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”
For His disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.
Then the woman of Samaria said to Him, “How is it that You, being a Jew, ask a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered and said to her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give Me a drink,’ you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

The woman said to Him, “Sir, You have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. Where then do You get that living water? Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank from it himself, as well as his sons and his livestock?” Jesus answered and said to her, “Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst. But the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life.”
The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water, that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw.”
Jesus said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”
The woman answered and said, “I have no husband.”
Jesus said to her, “You have well said, ‘I have no husband,’
for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband; in that you spoke truly.”
You have spoken the truth.
The woman said to Him, “Sir, I perceive that You are a prophet.
Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where one ought to worship.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, believe Me, the hour is coming when you will neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, worship the Father.
You worship what you do not know; we know what we worship, for salvation is of the Jews.
But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him.
God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”
The woman said to Him, “I know that Messiah is coming” (who is called Christ). “When He comes, He will tell us all things.”
Jesus said to her, “I who speak to you am He.”

At this point His disciples came, and they marveled that He talked with a woman; yet no one said, “What do You seek?” or, “Why are You talking with her?” The woman then left her waterpot, went her way into the city, and said to the men, “Come, see a Man who told me all things that I ever did.
Could this be the Christ?” Then they went out of the city and came to Him.
In the meantime His disciples urged Him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”
But He said to them, “I have food to eat of which you do not know.”
Therefore the disciples said to one another, “Has anyone brought Him anything to eat?” Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me, and to finish His work.
Do you not say, ‘There are still four months and then comes the harvest’? Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest!
And he who reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit for eternal life, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.
For in this the saying is true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’
I sent you to reap that for which you have not labored; others have labored, and you have entered into their labors.”
And many of the Samaritans of that city believed in Him because of the word of the woman who testified, “He told me all that I ever did.”
So when the Samaritans had come to Him, they urged Him to stay with them;
and He stayed there two days.

And many more believed because of His own word. Then they said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of what you said, for we ourselves have heard Him and we know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”
Now after the two days He departed from there and went to Galilee.
For Jesus Himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country.
So when He came to Galilee, the Galileans received Him, having seen all the things He did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also had gone to the feast.
So Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee where He had made the water wine.
And there was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum.
When he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to Him and implored Him to come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death.
Then Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will by no means believe.”
The nobleman said to Him, “Sir, come down before my child dies!”
Jesus said to him, “Go; your son lives.”
So the man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.
And as he was now going down, his servants met him and told him, saying, “Your son lives!”
Then he inquired of them the hour when he got better. And they said to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”
So the father knew that it was at the same hour in which Jesus said to him, “Your son lives.” And he himself believed, and his whole household.
This again is the second sign Jesus did when He had come out of Judea into Galilee.
After this there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
Now there is in Jerusalem by the Sheep Gate a pool, which is called in Hebrew, Bethesda, having five porches.
In these lay a great multitude of sick people, blind, lame, paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water.
(For an angel went down at a certain time into the pool and stirred up the water;
then whoever stepped in first, after the stirring of the water, was made well of whatever disease he had.)
Now a certain man was there who had an infirmity thirty-eight years.

When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he already had been in that condition a long time, He said to him, “Do you want to be made well?” The sick man answered Him, “Sir, I have no man to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up; but while I am coming, another steps down before me.”
Jesus said to him, “Rise, take up your bed and walk.”
And immediately the man was made well, took up his bed, and walked.
And that day was the Sabbath.
The Jews therefore said to him who was cured, “It is the Sabbath; it is not lawful for you to carry your bed.”
He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your bed and walk.’”
Then they asked him, “Who is the Man who said to you, ‘Take up your bed and walk’?” But the one who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a multitude being in that place.
Afterward Jesus found him in the temple,
and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you.”
The man departed and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
For this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus, and sought to kill Him, because He had done these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus answered them, “My Father has been working until now, and I have been working.”
Therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill Him, because He not only broke the Sabbath, but also said that God was His Father, making Himself equal with God.
Then Jesus answered and said to them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do; for whatever He does, the Son also does in like manner.
For the Father loves the Son, and shows Him all things that He Himself does; and He will show Him greater works than these, that you may marvel.
For as the Father raises the dead and gives life to them, even so the Son gives life to whom He will.
For the Father judges no one, but has committed all judgment to the Son, 23 that all should honor the Son just as they honor the Father.
He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
Most assuredly, I say to you, he who hears My word and believes in Him who sent Me has everlasting life, and shall not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.
Most assuredly, I say to you, the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God; and those who hear will live.
For as the Father has life in Himself, so He has granted the Son to have life in Himself,
and has given Him authority to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man.
Do not marvel at this; for the hour is coming in which all who are in the graves will hear His voice and come forth—
those who have done good, to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of condemnation.
I can of Myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge; and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will but the will of the Father who sent Me.
If I bear witness of Myself, My witness is not true.
There is another who bears witness of Me, and I know that the witness which He witnesses of Me is true.
You sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
But I do not receive testimony from man, yet I say these things so that you may be saved.
John was like a burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.
But the testimony I have is greater than John's testimony, because the work that the Father has given me to finish—the very works that I do—they bear witness of me, that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me, He has testified of me.
You have never heard His voice, nor have you seen His form, and you do not have His word abiding in you, because you do not believe Him whom He sent.
You search the Scriptures, for you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify of Me, yet you are not willing to come to Me that you may have eternal life.
I do not receive honor from men.
But I know you, that you do not have the love of God in you.
I have come in My Father's name, and you do not receive Me; if another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
How can you believe, who receive honor from one another, and do not seek the honor that comes from the only God?
Do not think that I shall accuse you to the Father; there is one who accuses you—Moses, in whom you have trusted.
For if you believed Moses, you would believe Me; for he wrote about Me.
But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My words? After these things Jesus went over the Sea of Galilee, which is the Sea of Tiberias.
And a great multitude followed Him, because they saw His signs which He performed on those who were diseased.
And Jesus went up on the mountain, and there He sat with His disciples.
The Passover of the Jews was near.

Then Jesus lifted up His eyes, and seeing a great multitude coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where shall we buy bread, that these may eat?” But this He said to test him, for He Himself knew what He would do.
Philip answered Him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may have a little.”

One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him, “There is a lad here who has five barley loaves and two small fish, but what are they among so many?” Jesus said, “Make the people sit down.”
Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
And Jesus took the loaves, and when He had given thanks He distributed them to the disciples; and likewise of the fish, as much as they wanted.
So when they were filled, He said to His disciples, “Gather up the fragments that remain, so that nothing is lost.”
Therefore they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves which were left over by those who had eaten.
Then those men, when they had seen the sign that Jesus did, said, “This is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world.”
Therefore Jesus, perceiving that they were about to come and take Him by force to make Him king, departed again to the mountain by Himself alone.
Jesus Walks on the Water (Matthew 14:22-33; Mark 6:45-52) Now when evening came, His disciples went down to the lake, and got into the boat, and started across the lake toward Capernaum.
And it was already dark, and Jesus had not come to them.
Then the sea arose because a great wind was blowing.
So when they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near the boat; and they were afraid.
But He said to them, “It is I; do not be afraid.”
Then they willingly received Him into the boat, and immediately the boat was at the land where they were going.

The People Seek Jesus On the following day, when the people who were standing on the other side of the lake saw that there was no other boat there, except that one which His disciples had entered, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with His disciples, but His disciples had gone away alone—
however, other boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they ate bread after the Lord had given thanks.
When the people saw that Jesus was not there, nor His disciples, they also got into boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.

Jesus the Bread of Life And when they found Him on the other side of the lake, they said to Him, “Rabbi, when did You come here?” Jesus answered them and said, “Most assuredly, I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.”
Do not labor for the food which perishes, but for the food which endures to everlasting life, which the Son of Man will give you, because God the Father has set His seal on Him.
Then they said to Him, “What shall we do, that we may work the works of God?” Jesus answered and said to them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in Him whom He sent.”

Therefore they said to Him, “What sign will You perform then, that we may see it and believe You? What work will You do? Our fathers ate the manna in the desert; as it is written, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
Then Jesus said to them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, Moses did not give you the bread from heaven, but My Father gives you the true bread from heaven.”
For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.
Then they said to Him, “Lord, give us this bread always.”
And Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.”
But I said to you that you have seen Me and yet do not believe.
All that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out.
For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
This is the will of the Father who sent Me, that of all He has given Me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up at the last day.
And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him may have everlasting life; and I will raise him up at the last day.”
The Jews then complained about Him, because He said, “I am the bread which came down from heaven.”

And they said, “Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How is it then that He says, ‘I have come down from heaven’?” Jesus therefore answered and said to them, “Do not murmur among yourselves.”
No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him; and I will raise him up at the last day.
It is written in the prophets, ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’
Therefore everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to Me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except He who is from God; He has seen the Father.
Most assuredly, I say to you, he who believes in Me has everlasting life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and are dead.
This is the bread which comes down from heaven, that one may eat of it and not die.
I am the living bread which came down from heaven.
If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever; and the bread that I shall give is My flesh, which I shall give for the life of the world.”

The Jews therefore quarreled among themselves, saying, “How can this Man give us His flesh to eat?” Then Jesus said to them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you.”
Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
For My flesh is food indeed, and My blood is drink indeed.
He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.
As the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
This is the bread which came down from heaven—not as your fathers ate the manna, and are dead. He who eats this bread will live forever.”
These things He said in the synagogue as He taught in Capernaum.

The Words of Eternal Life Therefore many of His disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying; who can understand it?” When Jesus knew in Himself that His disciples complained about this, He said to them, “Does this offend you? What then if you should see the Son of Man ascend where He was before? It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life.”
But there are some of you who do not believe.
For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who would betray Him.
And He said, “Therefore I have said to you that no one can come to Me unless it has been granted to him by My Father.”
Peter’s Confession of Faith From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more.

Then Jesus said to the twelve, “Do you also want to go away?” But Simon Peter answered Him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered them, “Did I not choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?”
He spoke of Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, for it was he who would betray Him, being one of the twelve.
After these things Jesus walked in Galilee; for He did not want to walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill Him.
Now the Jews’ Feast of Tabernacles was at hand.
His brothers therefore said to Him, “Depart from here and go into Judea, that Your disciples also may see the works that You are doing.”
For no one does anything in secret while he himself seeks to be known openly.
If You do these things, show Yourself to the world.”
For even His brothers did not believe in Him.
Then Jesus said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.”
The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me because I testify of it that its works are evil.
You go up to this feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, for My time has not yet fully come.”
When He had said these things to them, He remained in Galilee.
Jesus at the Feast But when His brothers had gone up, then He also went up to the feast, not openly, but as it were in secret.

Then the Jews sought Him at the feast, and said, “Where is He?” And there was much complaining among the people concerning Him. Some said, “He is good”; others said, “No, on the contrary, He deceives the people.”
However, no one spoke openly of Him for fear of the Jews.
Now about the middle of the feast Jesus went up into the temple and taught.
And the Jews marveled, saying, “How does this Man know letters, having never studied?”
Jesus answered them and said, “My doctrine is not Mine, but His who sent Me.”
If anyone wills to do His will, he shall know concerning the doctrine, whether it is from God or whether I speak on My own authority.
He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is true, and no unrighteousness is in Him.
Did not Moses give you the law, yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill Me?”
The people answered and said, “You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill You?” Jesus answered and said to them, “I did one work, and you all marvel.”
Moses therefore gave you circumcision (not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers), and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
If a man receives circumcision on the Sabbath, so that the law of Moses should not be broken, are you angry with Me because I made a man completely well on the Sabbath?
Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.”
Now some of them from Jerusalem said, “Is this not He whom they seek to kill?”
But look, He speaks boldly, and they say nothing to Him.
Can it be that the Jewish leaders have truly come to know that this is the Messiah? 27 We know where this man is from, but when the Messiah comes, no one will know where he is from.
28 Then Jesus, while teaching in the temple, cried out and said, “You know me, and you also know where I have come from.
I have not come on my own, but the one who sent me is true, whom you do not know.
But I know him, because I have come from him, and he has sent me.”
30 Hearing this, the Jewish leaders wanted to arrest Jesus, but no one laid a hand on him because his time for death had not yet come.

Nevertheless, many people in the crowd believed in him and said, “When the Messiah comes, will he perform more miraculous signs than this man has?” The attempt to arrest Jesus: 32 The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering about Jesus, so the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple guards to arrest him.
Jesus said, “I am with you for only a little while, and then I will go back to the one who sent me.
You will look for me, but you will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come.”

35 The Jewish leaders said to one another, “Where will he go that we cannot find him? Will he go to the Greeks living among the foreigners to teach them? 36 What does this mean? What he said, ‘You will look for me, but you will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come.’”
Rivers of living water: 37 On the last day of the festival, which is the most important day, Jesus stood up and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let them come to me and drink.
Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture says, ‘Rivers of living water will flow from within them, which gives eternal life.’
39 Jesus said this about the Holy Spirit, which those who believed in him were to receive, because the Holy Spirit had not yet been given, as Jesus had not yet reached his glory.
Then many in the crowd, hearing this, said, “Truly, this is the Prophet whom we were waiting for.”

41 And some said, “This is the Messiah.” But others asked, “Will the Messiah come from the region of Galilee?” 42 Does not the Scripture say that the Messiah will come from David’s descendants and from the town of Bethlehem, where David lived? 43 Finally, because of him, there was a division among the people.
Some of them wanted to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him.

The disbelief of the Jewish leaders: 45 Then the guards returned to the chief priests and the Pharisees, who asked them, “Why didn't you bring him?” 46 The guards replied, “No one has ever spoken like this man before.”

47 The Pharisees answered them, “Have you also been deceived? 48 Have any of the leaders or the Pharisees believed in him? 49 But this crowd, which does not know the law of Moses, is under a curse from God.”

50 Nicodemus, who was one of them and had met Jesus earlier, said to them, 51 “Does our law judge a man before hearing him and knowing what he is doing?” 52 They replied to Nicodemus, “Are you also from Galilee? Look in the Scripture and see that no prophet comes from Galilee.”
53 Then everyone went to their own homes.
Jesus went with his disciples to the Mount of Olives.
Early the next day, Jesus came to the temple again.
Many people came to him, and he sat down and began to teach them.

As he was speaking, the teachers of the law and the Pharisees brought a woman who had been caught in adultery, stood her before the people, and said to Jesus, 4 “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
In the law of Moses, he commanded us that such a woman should be stoned to death.
But what do you say about this woman?” 6 They said this to test Jesus, so that they might find a reason to accuse him.
But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with his finger.
When they kept asking him, he straightened up and said to them, “Let any one of you who has never sinned be the first to throw a stone at her.”
8 Then Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with his finger.
When the people heard this, the older ones went away first, followed by others one by one, because they knew they were all sinners, and only Jesus and the woman were left there.
Jesus stood up and said to the woman, “Woman, where are they? Did no one condemn you?” 11 She replied, “No one, Lord.”
Jesus said, “I also do not condemn you; go, and do not sin again.”

Jesus the light of the world: 12 Resuming his teaching in the temple, Jesus said to the people, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light that gives eternal life.”
13 The Pharisees said to him, “You are testifying about yourself, so your testimony is not true.”
14 Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is valid, because I know where I have come from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
You judge by human standards, I do not judge anyone.
If I do judge, my judgment is correct, because I am not alone; but the Father, who sent me, and I together judge.
In your law of Moses, it is also written that the testimony of two people is accepted as truth.
I testify for myself, and my Father, who sent me, testifies for me.”
19 They asked him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus replied, “You know neither me nor my Father; if you knew me, you would know my Father too.”
20 Jesus spoke these words while teaching in the temple treasury, and no one arrested him, because his time of suffering and death had not yet come.
Jesus' statement about himself: 21 Jesus said to them again, “I am going away, and you will look for me, and you will die in your sin.
Where I am going, you cannot come.”
22 The Jewish leaders said, “Will he kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?” 23 Jesus said to them, “You are born of this world, and I am from heaven.
You are of this world, I am not of this world.
That is why I told you that you will die in your sins; if you do not believe that I am who I am, you will die, and your sins will not be forgiven.

25 The Jewish leaders said to Jesus, “Who are you?” He said to them, “From the beginning of my preaching, I have been telling you, ‘Who I am.’” 26 “I have much to say about you and much to judge, but the truth is that I only speak what I have heard from the one who sent me, and that is what I tell the people of the world.”
27 They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.
Then Jesus said, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He.
I do nothing of my own accord, but I speak these things just as my Father has taught me.
The one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”
30 As he was saying these things, many believed in him.
The truth will set you free: 31 Then Jesus said to those Jews who had believed in him, “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples.
32 You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
They answered him, “We are Abraham’s descendants; we have never been slaves to anyone.
Then how can you say, ‘You will be free’?” 34 Jesus answered them, “I tell you the truth, whoever sins is a slave to sin.
A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains in the house forever.
Therefore, if the Son sets you free, you will be truly free.
I know that you are descendants of Abraham, yet you do not follow my words, and that is why you want to kill me.
I speak what I have seen from my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”
39 They answered him, “Our ancestor is Abraham.”
Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s descendants, you would do the works that Abraham did.
But now you want to kill me, who has told you the truth which I heard from God; Abraham did not do this.
You do the works of your father.”
They said to Jesus, “We were not born of adultery; we have only one Father, that is God.”
42 Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love me, because I have come from God.
I did not come on my own, but he sent me.
Why do you not understand my speech? Because you do not accept my word.
You are of your father the devil, and you want to fulfill the desires of your father.
He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him.
When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own nature, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
But because I speak the truth, you do not believe me.
Which of you can prove me a sinner? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe me? 47 Whoever is from God hears God’s words; you do not hear them because you are not from God.”

Jesus and Abraham: 48 Hearing this, the Jews said to him, “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have an evil spirit in you?” 49 Jesus replied, “I do not have an evil spirit,” but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and is the judge.
I tell you the truth, “If anyone keeps my word, he will never see death.”
52 The Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have an evil spirit.
Abraham died and the prophets also died, and you say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, he will never see death.’
53 Our ancestor Abraham died.
Are you greater than him? And the prophets have died too.
Who do you claim to be?” 54 Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing.
But my Father, whom you say is your God, is the one who glorifies me.
You do not know him, but I know him.
If I said that I did not know him, I would be a liar like you, but I know him and keep his word.
Your ancestor Abraham rejoiced to see my day; he saw it and was glad.”
57 The Jews said to him, “You are not even fifty years old, yet you have seen Abraham?” 58 Jesus said to them, “I tell you the truth, before Abraham was born, I am.”
59 Hearing this, the people picked up stones to kill Jesus, but Jesus hid himself and slipped out of the temple.
Passing by, he met a man who had been blind from birth.

His disciples asked him, “Teacher, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?” 3 Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but he was born blind so that the works of God might be shown.
We must do the works of the one who sent me while it is day.
The night is coming when no one can work.
As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
6 Saying this, Jesus spat on the ground, made clay with the saliva, and applied the clay to the blind man's eyes.
He said to him, “Go,” “wash in the pool of Siloam” (Siloam means sent).
He went and washed his face, and when he returned, he could see.

8 Then the neighbors and those who had seen the beggar begging earlier began to say to each other, “Is this not the one who used to sit and beg?” 9 Some said, “It is he,” while others said, “No, but he is like him.”
He said, “I am he.”

10 Then they began to ask him, “How were your eyes opened?” 11 He answered, “A man named Jesus made clay, put it on my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go, wash your face in Siloam,’ so I went and washed my face and could see.”
12 They asked him, “Where is that man?” He said, “I do not know.”
Pharisees investigate the healing: 13 They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees.
The day Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes was a Sabbath day.
Then the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight.
He said to them, "He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
Therefore some of the Pharisees said, "This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath."
Others said, "How can a sinful man do such signs?" And there was a division among them.
They said to the blind man again, "What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?"
He said, "He is a prophet."
But the Jewish leaders did not believe that he had been blind and had received his sight, so they called his parents.

And they asked them, "Is this your son, who you say was born blind? How then does he now see?" 20 His parents answered them, "We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind; 21 but by what means he now sees, we do not know, or who opened his eyes, we do not know."
He is of age; ask him, he will speak for himself."
22 His parents said these things because they feared the Jewish leaders, for the Jewish leaders had agreed that if anyone confessed that he was the Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.
For this reason his parents said, "He is of age, ask him."
24 So the Jewish leaders called the man who was blind a second time and said to him, "Give God the glory; we know that this man is a sinner."
25 He answered, "I do not know whether he is a sinner; one thing I know, that though I was blind, now I see."

26 Then they said to him again, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?" 27 He answered them, "I told you already, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become his disciples?" 28 Then they reviled him and said, "You are his disciple, but we are Moses' disciples."
We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this fellow, we do not know where he is from.
30 He answered them, "Why, this is a marvelous thing, that you do not know where he is from, yet he has opened my eyes!"
We know that God does not hear sinners; but if anyone is a worshiper of God and does His will, He hears him.
Since the world began it has been unheard of that anyone opened the eyes of one who was born blind.
If this man were not from God, He could do nothing.
34 They answered and said to him, "You were altogether born in sins, and are you teaching us?" And they cast him out of the synagogue.

Spiritual blindness 35 Jesus heard that they had cast him out, and when He found him, He said, "Do you believe in the Son of God?" 36 He answered, "Who is the Son of God, that I may believe in Him?" 37 Jesus said to him, "You have both seen Him, and it is He who is talking with you."
38 He said, "Lord, I believe."
And he worshipped Him.
And Jesus said, "For judgment I have come into this world, that those who do not see may see, and that those who see may be made blind."

40 Then the Pharisees who were with Him heard these words and said to Him, "Are we blind also?" 41 Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, 'We see.' Therefore your sin remains."
Jesus said, "Most assuredly, I say to you, he who does not enter the sheepfold by the door, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber."
But he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice; and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
And when he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
Yet they will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him, for they do not know the voice of strangers."
6 Jesus used this illustration, but they did not understand the things which He spoke to them.
Jesus the Good Shepherd 7 Then Jesus said to them again, "Most assuredly, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep."
All who ever came before Me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them.
I am the door. If anyone enters by Me, he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture."
10 The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep.
But a hireling, he who is not the shepherd, one who does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees; and the wolf catches them and attacks them.
The hireling flees because he is a hireling and does not care about the sheep.
"I am the good shepherd; and I know My sheep, and am known by My own."
As the Father knows Me, even so I know the Father; and I lay down My life for the sheep.
And other sheep I have which are not of this fold;
them also I must bring,
and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd.
Therefore My Father loves Me, because I lay down My life that I may take it again.
No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself.
I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This command I have received from My Father."
19 Therefore there was a division again among the Jews because of these sayings.

And many of them said, "He has a demon and is mad. Why do you listen to Him?" 21 Others said, "These are not the words of one who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?" The Unbelief of the Jews 22 Now it was the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter.
And Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon's porch.
Then the Jews surrounded Him and said to Him, "How long do You keep us in doubt? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly."
25 Jesus answered them, "I told you, and you do not believe.
The works that I do in My Father's name, they bear witness of Me. 26 But you do not believe, because you are not of My sheep.
My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me. 28 And I give them eternal life,
and they shall never perish, neither shall anyone snatch them out of My hand.
My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all; and no one is able to snatch them out of My Father's hand.
I and My Father are one."
31 Then the Jews took up stones again to stone Him.

Jesus answered them, "Many good works I have shown you from My Father. For which of those works do you stone Me?" 33 The Jews answered Him, saying, "For a good work we do not stone You, but for blasphemy, and because You, being a Man, make Yourself God."
34 Jesus answered them, "Is it not written in your law, 'I said, "You are gods"'?"

If He called them gods, to whom the word of God came (and the Scripture cannot be broken), 36 do you say of Him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, 'You are blaspheming,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'? 37 If I do not do the works of My Father, do not believe Me;
but if I do, though you do not believe Me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in Me, and I in Him."
39 Therefore they sought again to seize Him, but He escaped out of their hand.
And He went away again beyond the Jordan to the place where John was baptizing at first, and there He stayed.
Then many came to Him and said, "John performed no sign, but all the things that John spoke about this man were true."
42 And many believed in Him there.
Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.
It was that Mary who anointed the Lord with fragrant oil and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
