I will tell you something; your circumcision is only beneficial if you obey the laws; if you do not do so, you are like those people who have not been circumcised.
If those who are uncircumcised keep the precepts of the law, will God not call them His own people?
Those who are uncircumcised and keep God's commands will criticize you who have God's laws but do not obey them.
A person is not a true Jew who is only born of Jewish parents, and true circumcision is not that which is done outwardly in the flesh for show.
A person is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code; such a person's praise is not from people, but from God.
Someone might ask, what is the benefit of being a Jew or what is the benefit of being circumcised? There are many benefits of being a Jew, because the word of God was entrusted to the Jews.
If some Jews turn out to be unfaithful, what difference does it make? God is faithful in keeping His promises, so this does not mean that God is also unfaithful.

No! Absolutely not! Instead, God is true, and every person in the world is proven a liar, just as it is written about God in the Holy Scriptures, 'So that you may be proved righteous in your words and prevail when you judge.'
Therefore, if my evil deeds prove God's righteousness, what should we say? Should we say that if God brings wrath, is He unjust? (I am speaking from a worldly perspective.)

No! Absolutely not! If God cannot judge the Jewish people in the right way, how can He judge the people of the world in the right way? Can anyone say, if my lie shows God's truth and increases His glory, how can God judge me as a sinner?
Some people criticize me by saying, 'Let us do evil that good may result.' Those who say such things against me deserve punishment.
No One Is Righteous: So what can we say? Are we Jews better than the Gentiles? Not at all! Because we have already accused both Jews and Gentiles that they are all under the power of sin.
Just as it is written in the Holy Scriptures: 'There is no one righteous in God's sight, not even one.'
There is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God.
All people have strayed from the path of God, all of them have become worthless in God's sight, there is no one who does good, not one.
Their throat is like an open grave, from which a stench comes.
Because they speak evil with their mouths, and whatever words they speak are poisonous like the venom of a snake.
Their speech is filled with cursing and bitterness.
They are quick to shed blood; wherever they go, they bring destruction and distress; they do not know how to live with people in joy and peace.
There is no fear of God in them.
We know that whatever the laws of the prophet Moses say, they say it to those who are under the law, so that no person can make excuses, and all the people of the world may be held guilty before God.
Because no person will be righteous before Him by fulfilling the laws of the prophet Moses, because through the law, we come to know that we are sinners.

Righteousness Through Faith: But now, righteousness that comes from God without observing the law, and about which the laws of the prophet Moses and the books of the prophets have written long ago, is how God makes us righteous.
This means that we are made righteous by believing in the Lord Jesus Christ, which is for all people who believe in Jesus Christ.
Because in God's sight, all people are equal.

Because all have sinned and have fallen short of the glory of God; God showed grace to us, and through Jesus Christ, He redeemed us from the punishment of our sins and made us righteous without doing anything.
God sent Jesus Christ into this world to pay the price for our sins; Jesus Christ shed His blood and gave His life for us.

So that we may come to God through faith in Him, and He did this to show that He was righteous in His patience with sinful people in the past and in forgiving their sins, and now His righteousness is revealed, so that they themselves are made righteous, and whoever keeps faith in the Lord Jesus also becomes righteous in God's sight.
So can we boast about anything? There is no place for that.
By observing the laws or by fulfilling them? No! But we boast by believing in Jesus Christ.
Because of this, we have reached this conclusion that God makes us righteous through faith in Jesus Christ, not by following the rules and regulations of the Prophet Moses.
God is not only the God of the Jews, but He is also the God of the non-Jews.
Because there is only one God, who makes those who are circumcised righteous by faith in Jesus Christ and also those who are uncircumcised by faith.
So, does our faith render the laws and rules useless? No! Absolutely not! On the contrary, when we have faith, we understand why God gave us these rules and regulations.
So, as Jews, what shall we say about our ancestor Abraham?
If Abraham had been made righteous by good works, he could have boasted about it, but he cannot boast before God through good works.
What does the Holy Scripture say? It says, 'Abraham believed God's promise, and because of his faith, God declared him righteous.'
And the one who works, his wages are not considered a reward, but it is his right.
But a person is not made righteous by works; rather, the ungodly person who believes in God is made righteous because of his faith.
King David also refers to the one whom God makes righteous without works as blessed.
'Blessed are those whose transgressions are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.'
'Blessed is the man whose sins the Lord does not count against him.'
Is this blessing for those who are circumcised, or is it also for those who are not circumcised? We say, 'Abraham believed God, and because of his faith, God declared him righteous.'
So when did this happen? While in the state of circumcision or uncircumcision? Not in the state of circumcision, but in the state of uncircumcision.

Even when Abraham was not circumcised, God accepted him and made him righteous; the mark of circumcision is a seal of Abraham's belief, so Abraham is the spiritual father of those who have faith but are not circumcised, so that they might be made righteous through faith.
And he is the spiritual father of those who are circumcised, who not only are circumcised but also have the same faith as their father Abraham had when he was not yet circumcised.

Receiving the promise through faith. 13 God promised Abraham and his descendants the whole world; this did not happen because Abraham followed the law, but because he believed in God, for that reason He made him righteous.
If this promise was given to Abraham and his descendants because they followed the law, then faith would be useless and the promise would be proven false.
But God's wrath falls on those who do not follow the law, and where there is no law, there is no violation.

For this reason, the promise is received by believing in God, which is according to grace; this promise has been received by all of Abraham's descendants, not just those who follow the law of the Prophet Moses, but also for those who believe in God like Abraham, because Abraham is the father of all of us.
As it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'I have made you a father of many nations'; in the eyes of God, Abraham is our father.
He believed in the God who gives life to the dead and speaks of things that are not as though they are.
18-19 God said to Abraham, 'You will have many descendants.'
But Abraham thought, how will I have children in my old age? Because he was about a hundred years old, and Sarah was also too old to bear children.
From all these things it was clear that he could not have many descendants, yet Abraham's faith did not weaken; he continued to believe in God's promise and did not lose hope.
And he did not doubt God's promise by becoming faithless, but being firm in faith, he gave glory to Him.
And he knew for certain that what God had promised, He was also powerful enough to fulfill.
And because of his faith, God declared him righteous.
And this word of the Holy Scripture, 'Because of his faith, God declared him righteous,'
was not written only for Abraham, but also for us, for whom it was written, who will be made righteous through faith; that is, for us who believe in the One who raised our Lord Jesus from the dead.
Jesus Christ was handed over and killed for our transgressions, and God raised Him to make us righteous.
Therefore, since we have been made righteous by believing in Christ, we have reconciliation with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Through faith, Christ has brought us into this grace of the Father.
In this grace we stand, and we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering leads to endurance, endurance to proven character, and proven character leads to hope.
And hope does not lead to disappointment, because the love of God has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us by God.
Because when we were weak, Christ died for wicked people at the right time appointed by God.
It is difficult for someone to give his life for a righteous person, but perhaps for a good person, one might be ready to give his life.
But God proves His love for us in this way: while we were still sinners, Christ Jesus died for us.

Since we have now been made righteous in God's eyes by the shedding of Jesus' blood, why would we not be saved from God's wrath through Him? Because when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, and the best part is that because we are reconciled, our salvation is certain through the life given by His Son, Jesus Christ.
Now, through our Lord Jesus Christ, we have been reconciled to God, and for this, we rejoice in Him.

Death through Adam, life through Christ. 12 God created one man, Adam, because of whom sin entered the world, and because of that sin came death; and in this way, death spread to all people because, being descendants of Adam, all became sinners.
Even before the law of the Prophet Moses was given, people in the world were sinning, but that sin was not counted because there were no laws to be broken.
Yet, death came to everyone from Adam to the Prophet Moses.
We did not break the commandment the way Adam broke God's commandment, and Adam was a pattern of Jesus Christ, who was to come.

But there is a very big difference between Adam's transgression and the gift of God's grace, because even though many died due to the transgression of one man, Adam, God's grace has been poured out on many through another man, Jesus Christ.
So the result of God's gift is very different from Adam's sin.
His sin brings judgment, but God's gift makes us righteous, even if we are guilty of many sins.
Because death came to all through the transgression of one man.
But more than this, God's grace and the gift of righteousness are given to those who receive them; they triumph over sin and death through Jesus Christ, and they will reign in eternal life with Him.
Just as Adam's transgression brought judgment for all people, in the same way, by Christ Jesus doing the work of righteousness, all people received life, and they were made righteous in God's eyes.
Because just as many became sinners by the disobedience of one man, in the same way, many will be made righteous by the obedience of one man.
The laws of Moses were given to us so that people could see how sinful they are, but when people sin even more, God's grace becomes even greater than that.
All people sinned and died, but through our Lord Jesus Christ, God's grace makes us righteous and gives us eternal life.
Could someone say that God forgives our sins by His grace, but don't think that we should keep on sinning so that grace may increase.
No! Absolutely not! Since we have died to sin, we should not sin again.
We know that all of us who have been baptized in the name of Jesus Christ are such that we have died with Christ.

Because of this, when we are baptized, we die with Him and are buried with Him, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, God, in the same way we should also live a new life.
Because if we have become one with Him through baptism in the likeness of His death, then we will certainly also be one with Him in the likeness of His resurrection.
In this same way, our old sinful nature was crucified with Jesus Christ, so that the sinful nature in our bodies might be destroyed, and we would no longer remain in slavery to sin.
Because when we died with Christ, we became free from the power of sin.
Therefore, if we died with Christ, my belief is that we will also live with Him.
Because we know that Christ, having risen from the dead, will not die again; death will no longer have dominion over Him.
Because Christ died once for sin, but now that He lives, He lives to glorify God.
In the same way, consider yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
Therefore, do not let the desires of sin reign in your mortal bodies, and do not be in the control of its desires.

Do not use the parts of your body for works of unrighteousness, but knowing that you have been raised from the dead, give your lives to God, and present the parts of your body to God for righteous deeds.
Then sin will not have dominion over you, because you are not under the law, but you are living under God's grace.

Slaves of righteousness. 15 So what does this mean? That we are not under the law, but under God's grace, so can we sin? No! Absolutely not! 16 You know that when you offer yourselves to be someone's slave, you do whatever your master says.
You can be slaves of sin, which brings death, or you can obey God and live a life of righteousness.
You were slaves of sin, but now you have obeyed all the teachings that you received; for this, I thank God.
Now, being freed from the power of sin, become slaves of God so that you may do righteous deeds.
I write to you in an easy way so that an ordinary person can also understand easily, that when you were slaves of your past life, you were doing all kinds of impure and evil deeds.
So now, make your body a slave to a righteous life so that you can live a holy life.
When you were slaves of sin, you were not able to do righteous deeds.
You were doing evil deeds, and now you are ashamed of those deeds, so what did you get? The result of all these things is death.
But now, having been freed from sin and becoming slaves of God, you are doing things that make you holy, and the result is eternal life.
Because the result of sin is death, but God's gift is eternal life in our Lord Jesus Christ.
O believing brothers, you know (I speak to those who know the law) that as long as a person lives, he must follow the law.
For example, a married woman should stay with her husband according to the law until death, but if the husband dies, she is free from the law of the husband.

Therefore, if she becomes someone else's while her husband is alive, she will be called an adulteress, but if the husband dies, she is free from that law, to the extent that she will not be an adulteress even if she becomes someone else's.
In the same way, O my believing brothers, when you died with Christ, you died to the law; now you are Christ's, who was raised from the dead, so that we can live a righteous life for God.
Because when we live according to the desires of our flesh, the desires of sin work in our members, and the law exposes those desires and brings death.
We died to the law in whose bonds we were before.
Now we can serve God in a new way, following the Holy Spirit.

Law and sin. 7 So what do we say? That the law of the Prophet Moses is sin? No! Absolutely not! On the contrary, it is the law that tells me what sin is! If the law did not say, 'Do not covet,' I would not even know what coveting is.
But sin, finding an opportunity, produced in me all kinds of coveting through the commandment, because without the law, sin is dead.
There was a time when I lived without the law of the Prophet Moses, but when I knew the law of the Prophet Moses, the desire to sin started in me, and I became like someone dead.
And that commandment through which I was to find life became the cause of my spiritual death.
Because sin, finding an opportunity, deceived me through the commandment, and through it, my spiritual death also occurred.
Therefore, we have reached this conclusion that the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
So did the law of the Prophet Moses, which was good, bring death to me? No! Absolutely not! It was sin that did this.
But the law, which was good, brought death to me, so that the reality of sin might be manifested, and the commandment shows that sin is very evil.
The inner struggle of man. 14 Because we know that the law of the Prophet Moses is spiritual, but I am physical and a slave to sin.
And what I do, I do not understand, because what I want, I do not do, but I do what I hate.
If I do the evil things that I do not want to do, then I acknowledge that the law of the Prophet Moses is good.
So in this state, what does the evil things in me, it is not I, but it is the sin that dwells in me.
Because I know that in me, that is, in my sinful nature, no good thing dwells.
My soul wants to do good deeds, but I cannot do good deeds.
Because what good deed my soul wants to do, I do not do, but the evil deeds that I do not want to do, I do.
Thus, if I do what I do not want, then I am no longer the one doing it, but sin living inside me is doing it.
In this way I come to know the truth: when I want to do good, I do evil instead.
For inwardly, I take great pleasure in the law of God.
But another law is working inside me, which fights against the law of my sinful nature.
This law makes my inner self a slave to sin, which is still in my body.
What a wretched person I am! Who will free me from this sinful nature that brings me death? Thanks be to God through my Lord Jesus Christ!
Therefore, with my mind I want to obey God's law, but because of my sinful nature I am a slave to sin.
So now there is no condemnation for those who believe in Christ Jesus.
For the Holy Spirit will give you the life that comes from Christ Jesus, and he sets you free from sin and death.

For what the law of Moses could not do because of the sinful nature, God did: he sent his own Son in human form to be a sin offering, and through the sacrifice of his Son's body God broke the power of sin.

So that the requirement of the law of Moses might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the sinful nature but according to the Holy Spirit. For those who walk according to their sinful nature think about evil things, but those who walk by the Holy Spirit think about the things that please the Holy Spirit.
If you live according to your sinful desires, you will die; but if through the Holy Spirit you put sinful desires to death, you will live.
For living according to sinful desires means being hostile toward God, because it is not subject to God's law and cannot be.
And those who live according to sinful desires cannot please God.
But since God's Holy Spirit lives in you, you should not live according to sinful desires, but according to what the Holy Spirit says.
If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to God.
If Christ lives in you, the body is dead because of sin, but your spirit is alive because of righteousness.

If the Spirit of God, who raised Jesus Christ from the dead, lives in you, then the one who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal body through his Holy Spirit who lives in you.
Therefore, believing brothers, we are not debtors to the sinful nature, that we should behave according to it.
For if you live according to the sinful nature, you will die; but if by the Holy Spirit you put sinful actions to death, you will live.
For all the people who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God.
For you were not given a spirit of slavery to make you afraid; instead, the Holy Spirit makes us children of God, so that we call out, 'Abba, Father.'

The Holy Spirit himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. And if we are children, then we are heirs—heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ. If we suffer like Christ, we will also share in his glory.
The glory that will be seen in the coming time: I firmly believe that the sufferings and troubles of this present time are nothing compared with the glory that the Lord will give us.
For all creation is waiting with great expectation for the children of God to be revealed.
Everything God created lost its purpose, not because creation itself wanted it, but because God made it so; yet there is still hope.
Creation itself waits for the day when it will be freed from slavery to death and destruction and will share in the glory of God's children.
For we know that all creation has been groaning together and suffering pain until now, like a woman suffering birth pains before a child is born.
And not only God's creation, but we ourselves, who have the Holy Spirit living in us as a taste of the coming glory, also groan within ourselves.
This will happen when we are freed from the body and God adopts us as his children.
You were saved through the hope of the coming glory. If you hope for things you already have, then hoping is useless; no one hopes for something they already possess.
If we hope for things we do not yet have, we wait for them patiently until we receive them.
We do not know how to pray as we should, but the Holy Spirit helps us, because we do not know what we ought to pray for; the Holy Spirit himself intercedes for us with sighs beyond words.
God, who examines hearts, knows the purpose of the Holy Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the holy people according to God's will.
We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, that is, those who are chosen according to his will.
For those whom God chose beforehand, he also appointed to become like his Son Jesus Christ, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.
Then those whom he appointed beforehand he also called; those whom he called he also made righteous; and those whom he made righteous he also brought into his glory.

God's love. So what conclusion do we draw from these things? If God is on our side, who can defeat us? God did not hesitate to sacrifice his own Son for us, so why would he not also give us everything he promised? Who can accuse us before God? God himself is the one who makes us righteous.
Who can condemn us? It is Jesus Christ, who died and was also raised from the dead, and who is at God's right hand and also intercedes for us.

Who will separate us from Christ's love? Trouble, hardship, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, or the sword? As it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'For your sake people threaten to kill us every day; we are considered like sheep for slaughter.'
But in all these things we are more than victorious through the one who loved us.
For I know that nothing can stop Christ from loving us.
Whether we live or die, angels, rulers, powers in heaven, anything happening now or in the future, depth or height—none of these can separate us from God's love, which is in our Lord Jesus Christ.

If nothing can separate us from God's love, then why are the Israelites, my Jewish brothers, far from God? My heart is very sad for them. Even if I were blamed or separated from Christ for their deliverance, I would be ready for it. I speak the truth with Christ as my witness; the Holy Spirit and my conscience also testify that I am not lying.
They are the people of Israel, adopted by God; the glory, covenants, laws, right to worship God, and promises belong to them.
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, all the ancestors, also belong to them, and Christ, in human form, is also an Israelite from among them.
May the Most High God, who is over all, be blessed forever.
Amen.
But it is not that God has broken his promise, because not all the descendants of Israel are true Israelites.
Nor will all be his true children simply because they are Abraham's descendants; rather, the Holy Scripture says, 'It is through Isaac's descendants that your true children will be counted.'
That is, those born physically in the ordinary way are not God's children; they are the children of the promise.
For this is the word of the promise: 'Next year I will come again at this time, and Sarah will have a son.'
And not only this, but when Rebecca had twins by one man, our ancestor Isaac,

before they were born and before they had done anything good or bad, God told Rebecca, 'The older son will serve the younger.' God said this to show that he chooses according to his own purpose, not because of their good or bad deeds.
As it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'I loved Jacob more than Esau.'

So what shall we say? Is God's choice according to his own will unjust? No! Absolutely not! For God says to the prophet Moses, 'I will show mercy to whomever I wish, and I will have compassion on whomever I wish.'
Therefore, God chooses the person to whom he wishes to show mercy; his choice is not based on what people want or what they try to do.

For in the Holy Scripture God said to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, 'I made you king for this very purpose, so that I might show my power through you and that my name might be proclaimed throughout the earth.'
Therefore, he shows mercy to whomever he wishes, and he makes whomever he wishes stubborn.

God's anger and his mercy. Then many people will say to me, 'If this is so, how can God say that we are wrong? For who can stop God from doing what he wants?' O human being, who are you to argue with God? Can what has been made say to its maker, 'Why did you make me like this?' Does the potter not have the right over the clay to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor from the same lump? God wants to show his anger and power against those fit for destruction, but he is patient, because he wants to show how great he is and show mercy to those he has chosen to share in his glory.
That is, to us, whom he chose not only from among the Jewish people but also from among the non-Jews.
As he also says about the non-Jews in the book of the prophet Hosea, 'Those who were not my people I will call my people, and those whom I did not love I will love.'
And in the place where God had said to them, 'You are not my people,' there God will call them his children.
And the prophet Isaiah calls out concerning the people of Israel, 'Even if the descendants of Israel are as numerous as the sand of the sea, only a few of them will be saved.'
For the Lord will act quickly on the earth and will judge everyone in one act.
As the prophet Isaiah had said earlier, 'If the Lord of armies had not left some descendants for us, our condition would have become like Sodom and Gomorrah, which God completely destroyed.'
Israel's unbelief. So what shall we say? The non-Jews did not try to make themselves righteous, yet God made them righteous because they believed in Jesus Christ.
The Israelites who wanted to become righteous by obeying the law of Moses did not succeed in becoming righteous.
How could this happen? Because they wanted to become righteous through good deeds, as if by works, and not through faith.

They stumbled over that stone. As the Holy Scripture says about Jesus Christ, 'Look, I place in Jerusalem a stone that causes people to stumble and a rock that makes them fall; whoever believes in him will not be ashamed.'
Believing brothers, my heart's desire and my prayer to God for my Jewish people is that they may be saved.
For I testify about them that they have zeal for God, but not with proper understanding.
They failed to understand the righteousness that comes from God and tried to become righteous in their own way; they did not submit to God's righteousness.
For Christ has already fulfilled that purpose.
The result of the law that was given is that those who believe in Jesus Christ will be made righteous.
Salvation for everyone. For Moses wrote in the Holy Scripture about becoming righteous through the law: the person who obeys it will live because of it.

But the Holy Scripture says this about being made righteous through faith: 'Do not say in your heart, Who will go up to heaven to bring Christ down?' Or, 'Who will go down into the place of the dead?' (That is, to bring Christ back from the dead.) But what does it say? 'God's word is near you, so that you can confess it with your mouth and keep it in your heart.' This is the word of faith that we preach.
If you confess before people that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, God will save you.
For if we believe in our hearts, God makes us righteous, and if we confess with our mouths that we believe in Christ, we will be saved.
For Isaiah wrote in the Holy Scripture about Christ, 'Whoever believes in him will not be ashamed.'
There is no difference between Jews and Greeks, because God is Lord of all and saves everyone who calls on his name.
For the Holy Scripture says, 'Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
But how will people call for help from Christ if they have not believed in him? And how will they believe in someone they have not heard about? And how will they hear unless someone preaches to them?
If preachers are not sent, how will they preach? As the Holy Scripture says, 'How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!'
But not everyone believed that good news, as the prophet Isaiah says, 'Lord, who has believed our message?' Faith comes from hearing the message about Christ.

But I ask: did the Jews not hear about Christ? Surely they did, because the Holy Scripture says, 'Their voices have gone throughout the whole earth, and their words have reached the ends of the world.'

Then I ask: did the people of Israel understand the message about Christ? First, the Lord said through the prophet Moses, 'I will make you jealous through those who are not Jews; I will make you angry through a people you consider foolish.'
Then the prophet Isaiah speaks boldly about what the Lord said: 'I was found by those who were not looking for me, and I revealed myself to those who were not asking about me.'
But about the people of Israel, God also says through the prophet Isaiah, 'All day long I have stretched out my hands toward a people who disobey and argue.'
So I ask: has God rejected his people? No! Absolutely not! I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham and from the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not rejected his people, whom he chose beforehand.
Do you not know what the Holy Scripture says about the prophet Elijah? He complains to God against the people of Israel.
'Lord, they have killed your prophets and destroyed your altars; I alone am left, I who believe in you and am still alive, and they also want to take my life.'
Then God said to the prophet Elijah, 'I have kept seven thousand people for myself who have not bent their knees to worship the image of the god Baal.'
In the same way, at this time too, some Jewish people remain, chosen for God by his grace.
If they were chosen by God's grace, then it was not because of good deeds; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.

What was the result? The Israelites who wanted to be righteous in God's sight did not succeed, but those whom God chose became righteous with him; the rest became stubborn and refused to listen to him.
As the prophet Isaiah wrote in the Holy Scripture, 'God has given them a dull mind to this day, eyes that do not see, and ears that do not hear.'
And King David says, 'May what they eat become a trap for them, and may they fall into a pit like an animal; in the same way, these people will receive punishment from God.'
May their eyes become dark so that they cannot see, and may they remain bent under troubles all the time.
So I ask, have the Jewish people stumbled to their ruin forever? No! Not at all! But because of their disbelief, salvation has reached the Gentiles, so that Israel may be provoked to jealousy.
Now if their disbelief became a reason for the well-being of the Gentiles in the world, then why wouldn't the return of Israel's people to God be even better?
I am saying this to you Gentiles as an example of the salvation of other nations.
Since I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I take pride in my ministry, so that by any means I might provoke my own people to jealousy and save at least some of them.
For if their rejection as the people of Israel was the reason for the reconciliation of the Gentiles with God.
Then their acceptance by Christ will be like life from the dead for a person.

I give you an example, it is the custom of the Jewish people; when we knead flour, we first set aside a portion of the dough for God, then the whole batch is also for God; in the same way, if the root belongs to God, then the branches belong to Him as well.

The people of Israel are like the branches of an olive tree, and fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are like the root of the tree, but if some branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them, and you also benefited from the blessings meant for the Jewish people, just as the branch of an olive tree draws sap from the root of the tree.
So do not boast that you are better than those cut-off branches; remember that you do not support the root, but the root supports you.
Then you might say, 'God will cast me aside just like the branches broken off from the tree.'
So that He might embrace the Gentiles, who are like those branches that have been grafted in.
It is true that they were broken off because of disbelief, but you remain by faith, so do not be arrogant, but fear, for if God did not spare His own branches, He will not spare you either.
So consider the kindness and the severity of God! There is severity for the unbelieving, and kindness for you, if you do not continue in His kindness, you will also be cut off.
If the Jewish people start to believe again, they will be grafted back in, for God is able to graft them in again.

It is not natural for a wild branch to become part of a good tree, and those who are not Jewish are like a branch of a wild olive tree that is grafted into a good olive tree; however, the Jews are like a branch that grows from the good tree, so they can certainly be grafted back into their own tree.

The salvation of all Israel: 25 Brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, lest you be wise in your own sight; until the Gentiles come to God, some of the people of Israel will remain hardened.
And after this, all the people of Israel will find salvation.
As it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'The Deliverer will come from Jerusalem, and will remove ungodliness from the descendants of Jacob.'
And this will be My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.

28 The Jewish people became enemies of God because they did not want to believe the gospel; this was beneficial for you, but God loves them because He chose them for Himself; this is the promise He made to our ancestors.
For God never takes back His gifts and His calling.
There was a time when you Gentiles had rejected God, but now that the people of Israel have rejected God, mercy was shown to you for this reason.
Because mercy was shown to you, mercy will also be shown to them.
For God has consigned all people to disobedience; this is the reason why God treats them as prisoners, He does this so that mercy can be shown to everyone.

The praise of God: 33 Oh! How unfathomable are the depths of God's wisdom and knowledge! How great are His judgments! And how mysterious are His ways of working! 34 'For who can know the mind of God? Or who has been His counselor? 35 Or who has given anything to God, that it should be repaid to him?' No one.
For everything comes from Him, and He has made everything, and everything belongs to Him.
May His glory last forever, Amen.
Therefore, brothers and sisters, I urge you by the mercies of God, to present your lives as a living, holy, and acceptable sacrifice to God.
This is the right way to serve God.

Do not be conformed to the people of this world, but let God transform your thinking, and let your conduct also change, so that you may experience and know the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
For by the grace given to me, I say to everyone among you, do not think of yourselves more highly than you ought to think.
But instead, with a sound mind, think of yourself according to the measure of faith that God has given you.
For just as I have many parts in one body, and all the parts do not have the same function.
In the same way, we who believe in Christ have become parts of His body, and we are connected to one another.
According to the grace that God has given us, we have received different gifts.
So if someone has been given the gift of prophecy, let them speak the things that ensure that this is from God based on faith.
If one has the gift of serving others, let them continue in service; if someone is a teacher, let them continue in teaching.

The one who encourages, let them continue in encouraging; the one who gives, let them give with generosity; the one who leads, let them do it with zeal; the one who shows mercy, let them do it with cheerfulness.
Do not fake love, hate evil, and be eager for good.
Love one another as if you were of the same family, and honor one another above yourselves.
Work hard and do not be lazy, remain filled with spiritual zeal.
Continue serving the Lord with all your heart.
Rejoice in hope, be patient in affliction, and remain constant in prayer.
Help the holy people with whatever they need, and always be engaged in hospitality toward strangers.
Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
Care for others as you care for yourself; do not be arrogant, but keep company with the lowly; do not be wise in your own eyes.
Do not repay evil for evil; think about the things that are good in the eyes of all people.
As far as it depends on you, live in peace with everyone with all your heart.
Dear brothers and sisters, do not take revenge, but give God the opportunity to take revenge, for it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'Vengeance is My work, the Lord says, I will take it.'
20 But the Word also says, 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink, for by doing this, he will be ashamed of himself.'
21 Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Everyone should remain subject to the governing authorities, for all authority comes from God, and the authorities that exist have been established by God.
Therefore, whoever refuses to follow those who have the power to rule is opposing the law of God, and those who oppose will receive punishment.
For rulers are not a cause of fear for good works, but for evil ones.
If you want to live without fearing the ruler, do good, so that you may receive praise from him.
For he is God's servant for your good.
But if you do evil, fear, for he has the right to punish, and he is God's servant to punish those who do evil deeds according to his authority.
Therefore, be subject to them not only to avoid punishment but also for the sake of a clear conscience.
Therefore, pay taxes, for governing officials are God's servants and remain engaged in that duty at all times.
Therefore, pay what is owed to everyone; pay taxes to whom tax is due, tribute to whom tribute is due, fear to whom fear is due, and honor to whom honor is due.
Duty toward one another: 8 There is one thing for which you should be in debt, and that is your mutual love, for whoever loves another has fulfilled the requirements of God's law.

For in the laws of the prophet Moses, there are many commandments: 'Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not covet,' and whatever other commandment there may be, the summary of all is found in this one command: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.'
10 Love does not do harm to a neighbor; whoever loves fulfills God's law.

You should continue to love one another, for the time is coming when God will deliver us from this evil world; since we first believed in Christ, that time has now drawn near, so you should awaken from sleep and be vigilant.

Our time in the world is like a night that is ending, and the time for Christ's return is very near; therefore, we should leave behind the works of darkness and perform good deeds like the light, which can become our weapons to oppose evil.

Come! Let us start conducting ourselves properly, like those who live in the light; do not be like those who live in darkness, who engage in indulgence, drunkenness, adultery, licentiousness, quarreling, and envy.
Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ as armor, and do not make plans to fulfill the sinful desires of the flesh.
Accept those who are weak in faith into your fellowship, but do not argue with them about what they should or should not do.
One believes that it is right to eat everything, but the one who is weak in faith eats only vegetables.
And those who eat meat should not look down on those who eat vegetables, and those who eat vegetables should not judge those who eat meat, for God has accepted both.
Who are you to judge someone else's servant? Their success or failure is in the hands of their own master; instead, they will be made to succeed, for the Lord is able to make them succeed.
In this way, some people value one day more than another, and some people consider all days the same; in this way, everyone should be convinced in their own mind that what they think is right.
Whoever values a day does so to honor the Lord.
Whoever eats meat does so to honor the Lord, for he gives thanks to God, and whoever eats vegetables does so to honor the Lord and gives thanks to God.
For we all belong to the Lord.
None of us lives for ourselves, and none of us dies for ourselves, but we do it to please God.
If we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord; whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For Christ Jesus died and rose from the dead for this very reason, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
Why do you judge your brother in faith? Or why do you despise your brother in faith? God will judge us all.
For it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'The Lord says, as I live, every knee will bow before Me, and everyone will acknowledge Me as God with their own tongue.'
12 Therefore, each of us will have to give an account of our own work to God.
Do not be the cause of your brother's downfall: 13 Therefore, from now on, we will not judge one another, but you resolve that no one will be a cause for a brother in faith to sin.
I know and have full conviction in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself, but it is unclean for the person who considers it to be so.

If your brother in faith is troubled because of what you eat, then you are not walking in the way of Christ's love, for whom Christ died; do not let your brother in faith fall away from Christ because of what you eat.
Because of this, if you are doing something that is good in your eyes, but someone else considers it evil, do not do it.
For the kingdom of God is not about eating and drinking, but about righteousness and peace that comes through the Holy Spirit.
Whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and is also praised by people.
Therefore, let us pursue the things that lead to reconciliation and peace, and that build up one another's faith.
Do not destroy God's work for the sake of food.
All kinds of food are clean, but do not be a cause for sin for the person who is offended by that food.
It is better that you neither eat meat nor drink the juice of the grape, nor do anything else that would cause your brother's faith to be shaken.
If you believe that you are doing right, keep these things between yourself and God.
Blessed is the one who does not consider themselves guilty in the matter they believe to be right.
But now if you have doubt in your mind about whether to eat or not, and still you eat, you are committing a sin.
For you are not acting according to your faith, and if you do something that you are doubtful about, it is wrong, so it is a sin.

It may be that those of us who are strong in faith know that these things do not matter, but we do not do this to please ourselves; we have to consider the fears and doubts of those who think we are wrong.
Each of us should do good things with our brothers in faith, which please them and keep them strong in their faith.
For Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written in the Holy Scripture, 'The one who speaks evil of You has spoken evil of Me.'
3 Whatever was written in the Holy Scripture previously was written for our instruction, so that through the patience and encouragement that the Scripture gives us, we may find hope.
I pray that God, the giver of patience and encouragement, may help you live your lives in the way of Jesus Christ and dwell together with one another in peace.
So that all of you, together, may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Embrace one another just as Christ has embraced you, for the sake of the good news for all, so that men may praise God.
Therefore, I say that Christ became a servant to the Jewish people to confirm the promises given to our ancestors and to prove the truthfulness of God.
And that the Gentiles may also glorify God for His mercy, as it is written in the Holy Scriptures, 'Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles and sing songs to Your name.'
And again it says, 'Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.'
And again the Holy Scriptures say, 'Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and praise Him, all you peoples of every nation.'
And the prophet Isaiah says in the Holy Scriptures, 'A descendant of Jesse will arise, and He will rule over all nations; He will save the Gentiles.'
I pray that God, who is the giver of hope, may fill you with all manner of joy and peace in believing, so that your hope may abound through the power of the Holy Spirit.

The reason for writing with courage: My believing brothers, I am fully convinced about you that you yourselves are full of goodness, and you should know what you ought to do, and you are also able to teach one another.
Still, I have written to you boldly about certain matters.

This happened because of the grace that God has given me, that I, being a servant of Christ Jesus for the Gentiles, should minister the good news of God like a priest, so that I may present the Gentiles as an offering to God, with which He is pleased, whom the Holy Spirit has made holy people.
Therefore, I can boast about the service of God because of Jesus Christ.
For I want to speak with courage only about those things which Christ has made me capable of doing, so that through what I have said and done, the Gentiles may obey the command of God.

By the power given through the Holy Spirit, I have performed wondrous signs and miracles, because of which, from the city of Jerusalem all the way to the surrounding region of Illyricum, I have proclaimed the good news of Jesus Christ to all.
But it is my desire to preach the good news where the name of Christ Jesus has not been invoked, and not be like a builder who builds a house on another's foundation.
But as it is written in the Holy Scriptures, I wish to fulfill it: 'Those who have not reached the good news of Jesus Christ will see, and those who have not heard will understand.'
Paul's plan for his journey to Rome: Therefore, I have been repeatedly hindered from coming to you.

But now, in the city of Jerusalem and the region of Illyricum, I have proclaimed the word of God to those who had never even heard about Jesus Christ, and now I will come to meet you, which I have longed for for many years.

Therefore, when I go to the country of Spain, I will pass through your place, because I hope that I will meet you during that journey, and when I am refreshed by your company, you will help me go to Spain.
But for now, I am going to the city of Jerusalem so that I can give a gift to the holy people of God there.
For the people of the regions of Macedonia and Achaia felt it was good to collect a donation for the poor people of the city of Jerusalem.

They felt it was good, but they are also debtors to the people of Jerusalem, because the Jews have shared the spiritual matters of God with the Gentiles, so it is right that the Gentiles share their earthly things with the Jews.
Therefore, I am going to the city of Jerusalem to give the donation that I have collected, and after that, I will meet you in Rome and then go to Spain.
And I know that when I come to you, I will share the blessing of Christ with you.

My believing brothers, because of the faith in our Lord Jesus Christ and the love that the Holy Spirit has given us, I beseech you to pray to God wholeheartedly for me and with me, so that I may be saved from the unbelievers in the region of Judea, and the gift that I am taking to the city of Jerusalem may be a cause for joy for the holy people of God.
And by the will of God, I may come to you with joy and find rest among you.
I pray that God, the giver of peace, may be with all of you.
Amen.
I want you to honor Phoebe, who is our believing sister and a servant of the church in the city of Cenchreae.
Welcome her in a way worthy of the holy people of God, and help her in whatever matter she needs you, because she has been a benefactor to many, including me.
Greet my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, Priscilla and her husband Aquila.
They risked their own lives for my sake, and not only I, but all the churches of the Gentiles also thank them.
And greet also the church that meets in their house.
Greet my dear brother Epaenetus, who was the first to believe in Christ in Asia.
Greet Mary, my believing sister, who worked very hard for you.
Greet my fellow Jewish brothers, Andronicus and his sister Junia, who were in prison with me and are highly regarded among the apostles, and who came to Christ before me.
Greet my dear brother Ampliatus, who is my beloved in the Lord Christ.
Greet my brother Urbanus, who is my fellow worker in Christ, and my dear believing brother Stachys.
Greet my brother Apelles, who has proven himself true in Christ.
Greet the household of my brother Aristobulus.
Greet my fellow believing companion Herodion.
Greet those of the household of my brother Narcissus who believe in God.
Greet my believing sisters Tryphena and Tryphosa, who work hard in the Lord.
Greet my dear believing sister Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet my brother Rufus, whom the Lord chose for His own, and his mother, who is like a mother to me; greet them both.
Greet my brothers Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and all the brothers who are with them.
Greet my brothers Philologus, Julia and Nereus and his sister, and my brother Olympas, and all the holy people who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss in love.
All the churches of Christ greet you.
Final instructions: Now, my believing brothers, I beseech you to watch out for those who cause divisions and create obstacles contrary to the true teaching you have received, and stay away from them.
For such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own desires, and by smooth-talking words, they deceive the innocent.
The report of your obedience to God has spread to all men, so I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise for what is good and innocent for what is evil.
The God of peace will crush the powers of Satan and bring them under your feet.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Timothy, my fellow worker, and Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, greet you.
I, Tertius, who am helping to write Paul's letter, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, who is my host and of the whole church, greets you.
Erastus, the city treasurer, and our brother Quartus greet you.
I pray that the grace of our Lord Christ may be with you all.

Praise to God: Now, regarding the good news I have proclaimed to you, that is, according to the proclamation of the message of Jesus Christ which can strengthen you in faith, according to the revelation of that mystery which was hidden for ages past.

But now, revealed by the command of the eternal God and made known through the writings of the prophets to all the Gentiles, that they also may believe and become obedient, to the only wise God through Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever.
Amen.
Paul had established a church in the city of Corinth.
Many problems related to life and faith in Christ had arisen within it.
Paul the Apostle's first letter to the Corinthians was written to resolve those problems.
At that time, Corinth was an international city of Greece.
It was the capital of the Achaia province of the Roman Empire.
It was famous for its vast trade, luxury, culture, and many types of religions.
But it was infamous for its excessive immorality.
The apostle's major concerns were division in the church, immorality, illicit relationships, questions related to conscience, church management, the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and the resurrection.
Paul, with his deep spiritual knowledge, explains how these questions can be resolved through the good news.
In Chapter 13, Paul explains that of all the gifts received by God's people, the greatest gift is love.
This is the most important chapter of this book.
This letter is from Paul, who was called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and my believing brother Sosthenes is also with me.

I write this letter to the people of the church of God that is in the city of Corinth, and those whom God has set apart for Himself in Christ Jesus, and whom He has called to be His holy people, and to the names of all those who in every place serve our and their Lord Jesus Christ.
We pray that you may continue to receive grace and peace from our Father God and Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessings of Christ: I thank my God always for you, because of the grace of God that has been given to you in Christ Jesus, through which He has given you many blessings.
You have been enriched in every way in Christ Jesus, and He has given you every kind of spiritual gift so that you can teach others the knowledge of the Word and the good news.
The special ability you have received proves that the message about Christ Jesus is true.
Because of this, while you await the return of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Holy Spirit has given you every kind of spiritual gift.
God will strengthen you in faith until the end, so that you may be found blameless on the day of the return of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God will do this, for He is faithful to do what He says, and He has called you into the fellowship of His Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

Division in the church: My believing brothers, because of the authority given to me by our Lord Jesus Christ, I beseech you to be in agreement with one another, maintain unity so that there is no division among you, and remain united in one mind.
For my believing brothers, the people of Chloe's household have told me that there are quarrels among you.
What I mean is that some of you call themselves followers of Paul, some of Apollos, some of Cephas, and some of Christ.

What you are doing is not right; has Christ been divided? Was I, Paul, crucified for you? Were you baptized in my name? I thank God that, except for my believing brothers Crispus and Gaius, I did not baptize any of you.
So that no one can say that you were baptized in my name.
And yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; apart from them, I do not know that I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the good news, and I did not preach the good news to men with clever reasoning, lest the story of Christ's death on the cross be rendered useless.
Christ is the knowledge and power of God: For the story of the death of Christ Jesus on the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved, it is the power of God.
For God has said in the Holy Scriptures, 'I will show those who consider themselves wise that in reality their knowledge is full of foolishness, and they are fools.'

Where is the wise man? Where is the scholar? Where is the debater of this world? Has God not made the wisdom of the world foolishness? For God decided that because the people of the world could not know God through their own wisdom, He used the preaching of the good news through us so that He could save those who have believed in Him, but some people considered this foolishness.
The Jews themselves consider this foolishness, because they only believe in signs and miracles from heaven, and the Greeks are in search of wisdom.
But we preach Christ crucified, which is a cause of stumbling to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles.
But to those whom God has called, whether Jew or Greek, Christ Jesus is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than human strength.
My believing brothers, remember who you were when God called you; you were not many of you wise by human standards, nor mighty, nor of noble birth.
But God chose the foolish of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak of the world to shame the strong.
And God chose those who are low and despised in the eyes of the world.
Through them, God rendered useless those who are considered very important.
God did this so that no creature could boast before Him.
Because of what God has done, you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom, righteousness, holiness, and redemption from God.
So that, as it is written in the Holy Scriptures, it happens the same way: 'Let the one who boasts, boast in what the Lord has done.'
My believing brothers, I did not come to you with a display of clever speech or superior wisdom, but I came to tell you the message of God.
For I had decided that I would tell you nothing but Christ Jesus and His death on the cross.
I was with you in weakness and fear, trembling greatly.
And in my teaching and preaching, there was no seductive speech of wisdom, but the Holy Spirit powerfully revealed that the message I spoke to you is true.
So that your faith might not be based on human wisdom, but on the power of God.
The wisdom of God: Yet, to those who are strong in faith, I speak a message full of wisdom, but this is not the wisdom of this world or the wisdom of its perishing rulers.

But the wisdom that we speak is the wisdom of God, which was hidden; no one had been able to understand it until now; God had decided before the creation of the world that His wisdom would bring glory to us.
No one among the rulers of this world understood God's plan, because if they had known, they would not have crucified the glorious Lord.

As it is written in the Holy Scriptures, 'What the eye has never seen, and the ear has never heard, and what has not entered the heart of man, all these things God has prepared for those who love Him.'
But God revealed those things to us through His Holy Spirit, because the Holy Spirit searches everything, even the deep things of God.
Who among men knows the thoughts of a man, except the spirit of man that is within him? Likewise, no one knows the things of God, except the Spirit of God.
But God has given us His Spirit, and we do not think as the people of the world think; because of this, we can recognize the blessings that God has freely given us.
And we tell you these things; we do not speak of things taught by human wisdom, but we teach those things taught by the Holy Spirit to spiritual people.
But the physical person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God, because they are foolishness in his eyes, and he cannot know them because they are examined in a spiritual way.
The spiritual person examines everything, but he is not examined by others.
This is true, because it is written in the Holy Scriptures: who knows the mind of the Lord? But we believers know what is in the mind of Christ.
My believing brothers, when I was with you, I could not teach you spiritual things as I teach spiritual people, but I spoke to you like worldly people, because you are still like children in Christ.

I taught you the introductory teachings of the good news of God, just as someone feeds a small child milk, and I did not teach you deep words of the Word which are like bread, because you cannot accept them yet.
Because you still live according to the sinful nature of worldly people.
Therefore, even now there is jealousy and strife among you, so are you not like worldly people? You are like those people who do not belong to God.

For when one person says, 'I am a follower of Paul,' and another says, 'I am a follower of Apollos,' are you not like worldly people? Who is Apollos? And who is Paul? Only servants, through whom you believed in Christ.
We all did the work that the Lord gave us.
It is like a plant: I planted, Apollos watered, and God made it grow.
Therefore, neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God is everything, the one who causes the growth.
The one who plants and the one who waters have the same purpose, but each person will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For we are God's fellow workers, and you are God's field and the house that God is building.
According to the gift God gave me, I laid the foundation like a wise master builder, and another is building upon it.
But each person must be careful about what he builds upon it.
For the foundation that was laid is Jesus Christ; no one can lay any other foundation.

If a servant teaches the true doctrine of God, which God gave him, he is like that master builder who builds on the foundation with good materials, such as gold, silver, and precious stones; and if he teaches false doctrine, he is like one who builds on the foundation with wood, hay, and stubble.

So each person will watch his work to see how he has worked, because Jesus Christ will reveal it when He returns; it will be like the day when that material is thrown into the fire, and he will see how each one has worked, and then He will decide who has done good and who has done evil.
Whoever's house remains on that foundation will receive his reward.
If Christ decides that the work done is not right, Christ will not give a reward to that worker, but he will not lose the eternal life that God has given him.
Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him, because the temple of God is holy, and you are that.
Do not be deceived; if anyone among you thinks he is wise according to worldly matters, it would be better for him to become a fool himself so that he may become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in the sight of God, as it is written in the Holy Scriptures, 'He traps the wise in their craftiness.'
And it is also written that 'The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.'
Therefore, no one should boast about men, because everything is yours.
Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or the present, or the future, everything is yours, and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.
Men should consider us servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God, who explain the mystery of God to men.
Furthermore, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
But it is a very small thing to me that you or any human court should judge me; I do not even judge myself.
For my conscience does not convict me in anything, but I am not innocent because of this, for my judge is the Lord.

Therefore, do not judge anything before the Lord comes, for He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men's hearts, and then each will receive their praise from God.

Now, brothers and sisters, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us the meaning of the saying, 'Do not go beyond what is written,' so that you will not be puffed up in being a follower of one person over another.

Who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not? You already have all the spiritual gifts that are given to men. You think that you have become kings without our help, and you have become wealthy, but it would have been better if you had truly become kings, so that we could have reigned with you.
For God has put us apostles on display at the end of the procession, like those condemned to die.
We have been made a spectacle to the whole universe, to angels as well as to human beings.
We are fools for Christ, because we preach Christ.
You think you are wise because you have a relationship with Christ.
Many people think I do not have the authority to be an apostle, but you boast that you have the power of God.
People do not respect us, they respect you.
To this very hour we go hungry and thirsty, we are in rags, we are brutally treated, and we are homeless.
And we work hard with our own hands.
When we are reviled, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it.
When we are slandered, we answer kindly.
Even today, the people of the world do not respect us, because they think we are useless people.
I am writing this not to shame you, but to warn you, as my dear children, whom I love.
Even if you had ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
Therefore I urge you to imitate me.
For this reason I have sent to you Timothy, my son whom I love and who is faithful in the Lord.
He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which agrees with what I teach everywhere in every church.
Some of you have become arrogant, thinking that I will not come to see you again.
But I will come to you very soon, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only how these arrogant people are talking, but what power they have.
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.

What do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod of discipline, or in love and with a gentle spirit? If you do not turn from your bad behavior, I will come with strictness; but if you turn from it, I will come in love and gentleness.
It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that even pagans do not tolerate: A man is sleeping with his father's wife.
You should be distressed and grieving; those who have done this should be removed from your fellowship, yet you are proud of it.
Even though I am not physically present, I am with you in spirit, and I have already passed judgment on the one who did this.
When you are assembled as believers, remember that you have the authority of Jesus Christ, and consider me present with you in spirit.
When you have the power of God with you, hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day the Lord Jesus returns.
So that he may ask for forgiveness for his sins, and if the man asks for forgiveness, he will be saved on the day the Lord Jesus comes back.
Your boasting is not good. Don't you know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough?
In the same way, if one man continues to sin, others will start sinning too by watching him.

Just as the Jewish people remove the yeast from their houses before the Passover festival, in the same way, if you remove that immoral man from your group, you will become a new community of believers in whom there will be no one who sins deliberately, and God will cleanse your hearts from within if you believe in Christ, because Christ died for us so that He could set us free from our sins; He is like the lamb that the Jewish people sacrifice during the Passover festival.
Therefore, let us keep the festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
Which means that, just as you lived before becoming believers, leave that life behind and start following Christ, so that no wickedness can remain in your hearts.
I wrote to you in my previous letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.

I did not mean that you should have no association with the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy, or the swindlers, or idolaters, because to avoid such people, you would have to leave the world.

But my point is that if anyone who calls themselves a brother or sister is sexually immoral, greedy, an idolater, a slanderer, a drunkard, or a swindler, do not associate with them; do not even eat with such a person.
What business is it of mine to judge those outside the church? What do I have to do with others? But it is your responsibility to examine closely those who are in the church.
As the Holy Scriptures say, God will judge those who are outside.
Therefore, expel the wicked person from among you.
If any of you has a dispute with another believer, take your case before the holy people of God, not before a judge who is an unbeliever.

Do you not know that the holy people will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge the smallest cases? Do you not know that we will judge angels? Then how much more these worldly disputes? If you have worldly disputes, will you appoint as judges those who are of no account in the church? I say this to shame you.
Is it true that there is not even one wise person among you who can resolve disputes between brothers and sisters?
But instead, one believer drags another to court, and that too in front of unbelievers.

The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means you are not people of Christ; instead of this, why not rather accept injustice and suffer loss yourself? But you yourselves do wrong and cause loss, and that too to other fellow believers.

Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral nor idolaters nor adulterers nor male prostitutes nor homosexual offenders nor thieves nor the greedy nor drunkards nor slanderers nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, and you were sanctified, and you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
The body is for the glory of God. You say, 'I have the right to do anything,' but I say, not everything is beneficial, although I can do everything, but I am not a slave to anything.
You say, 'Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food,' which is true, but God will destroy both them.
In the same way, the body is not for immorality, but for the glory of the Lord, and the Lord is the guardian of the body.
In the same way, my body is also important, because just as God by His power raised the Lord Jesus, He will also raise us.
Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Then shall I take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!
Do you not know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is written in the Holy Scriptures, 'The two will become one flesh.'
And he who is united with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.
Flee from sexual immorality.
No other sin affects the body as much as sexual immorality does, for the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God, and you are not your own?
Because you were bought at a price; therefore, honor God with your body.
Regarding the matters you asked me about in your letter, it is good for a man not to marry.
But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband, so that they remain faithful to each other.
The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
The wife does not have authority over her own body but yields it to her husband, and in the same way, the husband does not have authority over his own body but yields it to his wife.

Do not deprive each other except for a short time by mutual consent, in order to devote yourselves to prayer, and then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
But this is my suggestion, not a command.
My wish is that all of you were as I am, single.
Each person has a gift from God; one has one kind, another has another.
To the unmarried and the widows, I say that it is good for them to remain single, as I am.
But if they cannot exercise self-control, they should marry, because it is better to marry than to burn with passion.

To the married, I give this command—not I, but the Lord: A wife must not separate from her husband. But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband, and a husband must not divorce his wife.
To the others, I say—this I say, not the Lord: If any brother has a wife who is not a believer and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
And if a woman has a husband who is not a believer and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.

For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified through his wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise, your children would be unclean, but as it is, they are holy. If this were not true, your unbelieving husband or wife would not be considered God's people, nor would your children, but now they are considered God's people.
But if the unbeliever leaves, let it be so. The brother or sister is not bound in such circumstances; God has called us to live in peace.

For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife? Walk according to the calling of God. Each person should live as a believer in whatever situation the Lord has assigned to them, just as God has called them.
This is what I teach in all the churches.
Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man uncircumcised when he was called? He should not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commands is what counts.
Each person should remain in the situation they were in when they were called.
Were you a slave when you were called? Don't let it worry you, but if you can gain your freedom, do so.
For the one who was a slave when called in the Lord is the Lord’s freedperson.
Similarly, the one who was free when called is Christ’s slave.
You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of human beings, but be slaves of God.
I say again, brothers and sisters, each person, as responsible to God, should remain in the situation they were in when they were called, whether married or unmarried.
Now regarding the unmarried, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy, and I advise you.
Because of the present distress, I think that it is good for you to remain as you are.
Are you pledged to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free from such a commitment? Do not look for a wife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned.
But those who marry will face many troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.
What I mean, brothers and sisters, is that the time is short. From now on, do not worry about whether you have a wife or not, but keep engaged in serving God.
Those who weep, those who are happy, and those who buy things should not think too much about these things, because worrying about all these things will distract you from serving God.
Do not hold onto the things of this world as if they were too precious, because everything in this world will pass away.
My wish is for you to be free from the desires of worldly life.
An unmarried man is concerned about the Lord’s affairs—how he can please the Lord.
But a married man is concerned about the affairs of this world—how he can please his wife.

There is also a difference between an unmarried woman and a married one; the unmarried woman is concerned about the Lord’s affairs, trying to be holy in both body and spirit, but the married woman is concerned about two things: how she can please her husband and how she can please God.
I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but for the sake of what is fitting and to help you serve the Lord with undivided devotion.
If anyone thinks that he is acting improperly toward his virgin daughter if she is getting past her prime, he should do as he feels; let them marry; he is not sinning.

But the man who has settled the matter in his own mind, and is under no compulsion, but has control over his own will, and has made up his mind to keep his daughter as a virgin, he is doing the right thing.
So then, he who gives his virgin in marriage does right, but he who does not give her in marriage does even better.
A woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, but he must belong to the Lord.
In my judgment, she is happier if she stays as she is—and I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
